١٣٩٦٧ — عن أبي إدريس عائذ اللّٰه بن عبد اللّٰه أنه دخل المسجد يومًا مع أصحاب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وكانوا أول إمارة عمر بن الخطاب، قال: فجلست مجلسًا فيه بضعة وعشرون، كلهم يذكرون حديث رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وفي الحلقة فتى شاب شديد الأدمة، حلو المنطق، وضيء، وهو أشب القوم شبابًا، فإذا اشتبه عليهم من الحديث شيء ردوه إليه، فحدثهم حديثهم. فبينما عائذ اللّٰه جالس معهم في حلقتهم أقيمت الصلاة ففرقت بينهم، فأقسم لي ما مرت عليه ليلة من الدهر، لا مرض شديد سقمه، ولا حاجة مهمة، أطول عليه من تلك الليلة رجاء أن يصبح فيلقاهم. قال: فغدا إلى المسجد فأقبل وأدبر فلم يصادف منهم أحدًا، ثم هجر الرواح فأقبل وأدبر، فإذا هو بالفتى الذي كان بالأمس يشيرون إليه بحديثهم يصلي إلى أسطوانة في المسجد. فقام عائذ اللّٰه إلى الأسطوانة التي بين يديه، فلما قضى صلاته أسند ظهره إليها، فجعلت أنظر إليه حتى علم أن لي إليه حاجة. قال: قلت: قد صليت أصلحك اللّٰه؟ فقال الفتى: نعم. قلت: فقمت فجلست مقابله محتبيا، لا هو يحدثني شيئًا ولا أنا أبدأه بشيء، حتى ظننت أن الصلاة مفرقة بيننا. قال: قلت: أصلحك اللّٰه، حدثني، فواللّٰه إني لأحبك وأحب حديثك. قال: آللّٰه إنك لتحبني وتحب حديثي؟ قلت: واللّٰه الذي لا إله إلا هو إني لأحبك وأحب حديثك. فقال الفتى: لم تحبني وتحب حديثي؟ واللّٰه ما بيني وبينك قرابة، ولا أعطيتك مالًا. قال: قلت: أحبك من جلال اللّٰه. قال له: إنك لتحبني من جلال اللّٰه؟ قلت له: واللّٰه لأحبك من جلال اللّٰه. قال: فأخذ بحبوتي فبسطها إليه حتى أدناني منه، ثم قال: أبشر، فإني سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((إن الذين يتحابون بجلال اللّٰه في ظل عرش اللّٰه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله)).
فلما حدثني بهذا الحديث أقيمت الصلاة. قال: قلت: من أنت يا عبد اللّٰه؟ قال: معاذ بن جبل. وكان عائذ اللّٰه يكثر أن يحدث حديث معاذ بن جبل.
حسن: رواه البزار (٢٦٧٢)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٠/٧٨).

13967 — Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidh Allāh ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
One day, during the early period of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s caliphate, he entered the mosque and found a gathering of more than twenty of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They were all discussing hadiths of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Among them was a young man with a dark complexion, pleasant speech, a radiant appearance, and he was the youngest among them. Whenever something in the hadith became unclear to them, they referred it back to him, and he would clarify it for them.
While ʿĀʾidh Allāh was sitting with them, the prayer was established and the gathering dispersed.
He said:
“By Allah, no night that ever passed over me—not even one of severe illness or an urgent need—felt longer than that night, because I was hoping morning would come so that I could meet them again.”
In the morning he went to the mosque, walking back and forth, but did not find any of them.
Later, he returned early and saw the same young man whom they had been referring to the day before, praying beside a pillar in the mosque.
ʿĀʾidh Allāh stood by the pillar in front of him. When the young man finished praying, he leaned his back against it.
I kept looking at him until he realized that I needed something from him.
I said:
“Have you finished your prayer, may Allah rectify you?”
The young man replied:
“Yes.”
I sat opposite him with my knees drawn up. Neither did he say anything to me, nor did I begin speaking, until I thought the prayer might separate us.
Then I said:
“May Allah rectify you, narrate to me. By Allah, I love you and I love your narrations.”
He asked:
“By Allah, do you truly love me and love my narrations?”
I replied:
“By Allah, besides whom there is no deity, I truly love you and love your narrations.”
The young man asked:
“Why do you love me and my narrations? By Allah, there is no kinship between you and me, nor have I ever given you wealth.”
I replied:
“I love you because of the Majesty of Allah.”
He asked:
“Do you truly love me because of the Majesty of Allah?”
I replied:
“By Allah, I love you because of the Majesty of Allah.”
He then took hold of the cloth wrapped around my knees and pulled it toward himself until he brought me close.
Then he said:
“Rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘Indeed, those who love one another for the Majesty of Allah will be beneath the shade of Allah’s Throne on a day when there will be no shade except His shade.’”
When he had narrated this hadith to me, the prayer was established.
I asked:
“Who are you, O servant of Allah?”
He replied:
“Muʿādh ibn Jabal.”
ʿĀʾidh Allāh thereafter frequently narrated this hadith of Muʿādh ibn Jabal.
Good: Narrated by al-Bazzār (2672) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (20/78).

Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (22064), and this is his wording, al-Tirmidhī (2390), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (577).

١٣٩٦٨ — عن أبي مسلم الخولاني قال: أتيت مسجد أهل دمشق، فإذا حلقة فيها كهول من أصحاب النبي ﷺ، وإذا شاب فيهم أكحل العين، براق الثنايا، كلما اختلفوا في شيء ردوه إلى الفتى، فإذا شاب. قال: قلت لجليس لي: من هذا؟ قال: هذا معاذ بن جبل. قال: فجئت من العشي فلم يحضروا. قال: فغدوت من الغد، قال: فلم يجيئوا، فرحت، فإذا أنا بالشاب يصلي إلى سارية، فركعت، ثم تحولت إليه. قال: فسلم، فدنوت منه، فقلت: إني لأحبك في اللّٰه. قال: فمدني إليه، قال: كيف قلت؟ قلت: إني لأحبك في اللّٰه. قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يحكي عن ربه يقول:
((المتحابون في اللّٰه على منابر من نور في ظل العرش يوم لا ظل إلا ظله)).
قال: فخرجت حتى لقيت عبادة بن الصامت، فذكرت له حديث معاذ بن جبل، فقال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يحكي عن ربه عز وجل يقول:
((حقت محبتي للمتحابين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتباذلين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتزاورين فيَّ، والمتحابون في اللّٰه على منابر من نور في ظل العرش يوم لا ظل إلا ظله)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٢٠٦٤) - واللفظ له -، والترمذي (٢٣٩٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥٧٧).
13968 — Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī narrated:
I came to the mosque of the people of Damascus and saw a gathering containing elderly men from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.
Among them was a young man with dark-lined eyes and bright teeth. Whenever they differed concerning something, they referred it to that young man.
I asked the man sitting beside me:
“Who is this?”
He replied:
“This is Muʿādh ibn Jabal.”
I came later that evening, but they were not there.
The next morning I returned, but they still had not arrived.
Later, I came back and saw the young man praying beside a pillar. I prayed, then moved closer to him.
He gave salām, and I approached him and said:
“Indeed, I love you for the sake of Allah.”
He pulled me closer and asked:
“What did you say?”
I replied:
“Indeed, I love you for the sake of Allah.”
He said:
“I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrating from his Lord: ‘Those who love one another for the sake of Allah will be upon pulpits of light beneath the shade of the Throne on a day when there will be no shade except His shade.’”
I then left until I met ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and mentioned to him the hadith of Muʿādh ibn Jabal.
He said:
“I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrating from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic:
‘My love has become obligatory for those who love one another for My sake. My love has become obligatory for those who give generously to one another for My sake. My love has become obligatory for those who visit one another for My sake. And those who love one another for the sake of Allah will be upon pulpits of light beneath the shade of the Throne on a day when there will be no shade except His shade.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (22064), and this is his wording, al-Tirmidhī (2390), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (577).

Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ called ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah al-Sulamī and said:

13974 — Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever gives for the sake of Allah, withholds for the sake of Allah, loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, and gives in marriage for the sake of Allah has perfected his faith.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2521), Imām Aḥmad (15638), and al-Ḥākim (2/164).
The words:
“Whoever loves for the sake of Allah”
mean that he loves someone because of Allah, not merely because of his own heart’s personal inclination toward that person.
And the words:
“Whoever hates for the sake of Allah”
mean because of a person’s disbelief, innovation, or distance from the path of the Salaf, not because of personal harm or injury caused by that person.

١٣٩٧٥ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((إن أرواح المؤمنين لتلتقي على مسيرة يوم، ما رأى أحدهم صاحبه قط)).
حسن: رواه ابن وهب في الجامع (ص ٢٧)، وأحمد (٦٦٣٦)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٢٦١).

13975 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, the souls of the believers meet one another from a distance of a day’s journey, even though one of them may never have seen his companion before.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Wahb in al-Jāmiʿ (p. 27), Aḥmad (6636), and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (261).

١٣٩٧٦ — عن خزيمة بن ثابت قال: رأيت في المنام أني أسجد على جبهة النبي ﷺ، فأخبرت بذلك رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((إن الروح لتلقى الروح)).
وأقنع النبي ﷺ رأسه هكذا، فوضع جبهته على جبهة النبي ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢١٨٦٤)، وابن أبي شيبة (١١/٧٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٤/٩٧).

13976 — Khuzaymah ibn Thābit narrated:
I saw in a dream that I was prostrating upon the forehead of the Prophet ﷺ.
I informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of this, and he said:
“Indeed, one soul meets another soul.”
The Prophet ﷺ then tilted his head back in this manner, and Khuzaymah placed his forehead upon the forehead of the Prophet ﷺ.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (21864), Ibn Abī Shaybah (11/78), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (4/97).

١٣٩٧٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن اللّٰه إذا أحب عبدًا دعا جبريل فقال: إني أحب فلانًا فأحبه، قال: فيحبه جبريل، ثم ينادي في السماء فيقول: إن اللّٰه يحب فلانًا فأحبوه، فيحبه أهل السماء، قال: ثم يوضع له القبول في الأرض، وإذا أبغض عبدًا دعا جبريل فيقول: إني أبغض فلانًا فأبغضه، قال: فيبغضه جبريل، ثم ينادي في أهل السماء: إن اللّٰه يبغض فلانًا فأبغضوه، قال: فيبغضونه، ثم توضع له البغضاء في الأرض)).
متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (٢٦٣٧)، والبخاري (٧٤٨٥).

13977 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibrīl and says: ‘Indeed, I love so-and-so, so love him.’ Then Jibrīl loves him. After that, he announces in the heaven: ‘Indeed, Allah loves so-and-so, so love him,’ and the inhabitants of heaven love him. Then acceptance is placed for him on the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He calls Jibrīl and says: ‘Indeed, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.’ Then Jibrīl hates him. After that, he announces among the inhabitants of heaven: ‘Indeed, Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.’ Then they hate him, and hatred is placed for him on the earth.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (2637) and al-Bukhārī (7485).

١٣٩٨٠ — عن مجاهد قال: لقيني رجل من أصحاب النبي ﷺ فأخذ بمنكبي من ورائي، قال: أما إني أحبك، قال: أحبك الذي أحببتني له. فقال: لولا أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((إذا أحب الرجل الرجل فليخبره أنه أحبه)).
ما أخبرتك. قال: ثم أخذ يعرض علي الخطبة، قال: أما إن عندنا جارية، أما إنها عوراء.
حسن: رواه البخاري في الأدب المفرد (٥٤٣).

13980 — Mujāhid narrated:
A man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ met me and took hold of my shoulder from behind.
He said:
“Indeed, I love you.”
I replied:
“May the One for whose sake you love me love you.”
He said:
“Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not said, ‘If a man loves another man, let him tell him that he loves him,’ I would not have told you.”
Then he began offering me a marriage proposal and said:
“We have a slave girl, though she is one-eyed.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (543).

١٣٩٨٢ — عن ابن عمر قال: بينا أنا جالس عند النبي ﷺ إذ أتاه رجل فسلم عليه، ثم ولى عنه، فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إني لأحب هذا للّٰه. قال:
((فهل أعلمته ذاك؟)).
قلت: لا.
قال:
((فأعلم ذاك أخاك)).
قال: فاتبعته فأدركته، فأخذت بمنكبه فسلمت عليه، وقلت: واللّٰه إني لأحبك للّٰه. قال هو: واللّٰه إني لأحبك للّٰه. قلت: لولا النبي ﷺ أمرني أن أعلمك لم أفعل.
حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٥٦٩)، والطبراني في الأوسط - مجمع البحرين (٤٩٨٩)، وفي الكبير (١٢/٣٦٦).

13982 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
While I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came to him, greeted him with salām, and then left.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, indeed I love this man for the sake of Allah.”
He asked:
“Have you informed him of that?”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
“Then inform your brother.”
So I followed him until I caught up with him, took hold of his shoulder, greeted him with salām, and said:
“By Allah, I love you for the sake of Allah.”
He replied:
“By Allah, I also love you for the sake of Allah.”
I said:
“Had the Prophet ﷺ not commanded me to tell you, I would not have done so.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (569), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, as cited in Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (4989), and in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12/366).

١٣٩٨٤ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن رجلًا زار أخًا له في قرية أخرى، فأرصد اللّٰه له على مدرجته ملكًا، فلما أتى عليه قال: أين تريد؟ قال: أريد أخًا لي في هذه القرية. قال: هل لك عليه من نعمة تربها؟ قال: لا، غير أني أحببته في اللّٰه عز وجل. قال: فإني رسول اللّٰه إليك بأن اللّٰه قد أحبك كما أحببته فيه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٦٧).
قوله: “تربها” أي: تقوم بإصلاحها، وتنهض إليه بسبب ذلك.

english_source:
13984 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“A man visited a brother of his in another village. Allah placed an angel in wait for him along his path. When the man reached him, the angel asked, ‘Where are you going?’ He replied, ‘I am going to visit a brother of mine in this village.’ The angel asked, ‘Do you have some favor with him that you are seeking to maintain or improve?’ He replied, ‘No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.’ The angel said, ‘I am a messenger from Allah to you, informing you that Allah has loved you just as you loved him for His sake.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2567).
The word:
“tarubbuhā”
means that you are attending to or maintaining some favor and are going to him because of that.

١٣٩٨٥ — عن أنس، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((ما من عبد مسلم أتى أخاه يزوره في اللّٰه إلا ناداه مناد من السماء: أن طبت، وطابت لك الجنة، وإلا قال اللّٰه في ملكوت عرشه: عبدي زار في، وعلي قراه، فلم يرض اللّٰه له بثواب دون الجنة)).
حسن: رواه البزار (٦٤٦٦)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٣/١٠٧)، وأبو يعلى (٤١٤٠).

13985 — Anas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“No Muslim servant goes to visit his brother for the sake of Allah except that a caller from heaven calls out: ‘May you be blessed, and may Paradise be blessed for you.’ And Allah says in the dominion of His Throne: ‘My servant has visited for My sake, so his hospitality is upon Me.’ Allah is not pleased to give him any reward less than Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bazzār (6466), Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah (3/107), and Abū Yaʿlā (4140).

١٣٩٨٦ — عن ثوبان مولى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((عائد المريض في مخرفة الجنة حتى يرجع)).
وفي رواية:
((خرفة الجنة)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٦٨: ٣٩-٤١).
ورواه (٢٥٦٨: ٤٢) من طريق آخر عن ثوبان، مولى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((من عاد مريضًا لم يزل في خرفة الجنة)).
قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه، وما خرفة الجنة؟
قال:
((جناها)).
وقد كان النبي ﷺ يعود المرضى لمعرفة أحوالهم وتسليتهم كما في الحديث الآتي:

english_source:
13986 — Thawbān, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The one who visits a sick person remains in the fruit-garden of Paradise until he returns.”
In another narration:
“In the harvested fruits of Paradise.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2568:39–41).
Muslim (2568:42) also narrated through another route from Thawbān, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever visits a sick person continues to remain in the khurfah of Paradise.”
It was asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what is the khurfah of Paradise?”
He replied:
“Its harvested fruits.”
The Prophet ﷺ used to visit the sick in order to learn about their condition and comfort them, as in the following hadith:

١٣٩٨٧ — عن جبير بن مطعم قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اذهبوا بنا إلى بني واقف، نعود ذلك البصير)).
قال سفيان: حي من الأنصار، وكان محجوب البصر.
صحيح: رواه البزار - كشف الأستار (١٩٢٠)، والطحاوي في شرح المشكل (٤٣٥٦).

13987 — Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Come with us to Banū Wāqif so that we may visit that blind man.”
Sufyān said:
“Banū Wāqif were a clan from the Anṣār, and the man had lost his eyesight.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1920) and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ al-Mushkil (4356).

((فأنت مع من أحببت)).

13989 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who loves a people but has not reached their level?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“A person will be with those whom he loves.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7169) and Muslim (2640).

١٣٩٩١ — عن أبي ذر أنه قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، الرجل يحب القوم، ولا يستطيع أن يعمل مثلهم.
قال:
((أنت يا أبا ذر مع من أحببت)).
قال: فإني أحب اللّٰه ورسوله.
قال:
((فإنك مع من أحببت)).
قال: فأعادها أبو ذر، فأعادها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥١٢٦)، وأحمد (٢١٣٧٩، ٢١٤٦٣)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٣٥١).

english_source:
13991 — Abū Dharr said:
“O Messenger of Allah, a man loves a people but is unable to perform deeds like theirs.”
He replied:
“O Abū Dharr, you will be with those whom you love.”
Abū Dharr said:
“Indeed, I love Allah and His Messenger.”
He replied:
“Then you will be with those whom you love.”
Abū Dharr repeated it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated the same answer.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5126), Aḥmad (21379, 21463), and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (351).

13992 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
I saw the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejoice over something more intensely than I had ever seen them rejoice over anything else.
A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, a man loves another because of the righteous deeds he performs, although he himself does not perform deeds equal to his?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“A person will be with those whom he loves.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5127).

١٣٩٩٣ — عن أبي هريرة، بحديث يرفعه، قال:
((الناس معادن كمعادن الفضة والذهب، خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا، والأرواح جنود مجندة، فما تعارف منها ائتلف، وما تناكر منها اختلف)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٣٨: ١٦٠).

13993 — Abū Hurayrah narrated a hadith which he attributed to the Prophet ﷺ:
“People are like mines of silver and gold. The best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding. Souls are like conscripted soldiers: those among them that recognize one another become harmonious, while those that are unfamiliar with one another differ.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2638:160).

١٣٩٩٣ — عن أبي هريرة، بحديث يرفعه، قال:
((الناس معادن كمعادن الفضة والذهب، خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا، والأرواح جنود مجندة، فما تعارف منها ائتلف، وما تناكر منها اختلف)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٣٨: ١٦٠).
13993 — Abū Hurayrah narrated a hadith which he attributed to the Prophet ﷺ:
“People are like mines of silver and gold. The best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding. Souls are like conscripted soldiers: those among them that recognize one another become harmonious, while those that are unfamiliar with one another differ.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2638:160).

13997 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever angers Allah in order to please people, Allah becomes angry with him and causes those whom he pleased through Allah’s displeasure to become angry with him. And whoever pleases Allah despite people’s displeasure, Allah becomes pleased with him and causes those who were angered by his seeking Allah’s pleasure to become pleased with him, until He makes him, his words, and his deeds appear beautiful in their eyes.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (11/268).

١٣٩٩٨ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((إن أوليائي يوم القيامة المتقون، وإن كان نسب أقرب من نسب، فلا يأتيني الناس بالأعمال، وتأتون بالدنيا تحملونها على رقابكم، فتقولون: يا محمد! فأقول هكذا وهكذا: لا)).
وأعرض في كلا عطفيه.
حسن: رواه البخاري في الأدب المفرد (٨٩٧).

13998 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, those closest to me on the Day of Resurrection are the people of taqwā, even if some lineage is closer to me than another. Let not other people come to me carrying righteous deeds while you come carrying the worldly life upon your necks, saying: ‘O Muḥammad!’ Then I will say like this and like this: ‘No.’”
He then turned away on both sides.
Good: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (897).

arabic_source:
١٣٩٩٩ — عن المعرور بن سويد، عن أبي ذر، قال: رأيت عليه بردًا، وعلى غلامه بردًا، فقلت: لو أخذت هذا فلبسته كانت حلة، وأعطيته ثوبًا آخر. فقال: كان بيني وبين رجل كلام، وكانت أمه أعجمية، فنلت منها، فذكرني إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال لي:
((أساببت فلانًا؟)).
قلت: نعم.
قال:
((أنلت من أمه؟)).
قلت: نعم.
قال:
((إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية)).
قلت: على حين ساعتي هذه من كبر السن؟
قال:
((نعم، هم إخوانكم، جعلهم اللّٰه تحت أيديكم، فمن جعل اللّٰه أخاه تحت يده، فليطعمه مما يأكل، وليلبسه مما يلبس، ولا يكلفه من العمل ما يغلبه، فإن كلفه ما يغلبه فليعنه عليه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠٥٠)، ومسلم (١٦٦١).
ورواه أبو داود (٥١٥٧) من طريق آخر، وزاد فيه:
((فمن لم يلائمكم فبيعوه، ولا تعذبوا خلق اللّٰه)).
وإسناده صحيح.

13999 — Al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd narrated from Abū Dharr:
I saw Abū Dharr wearing a cloak, while his servant was wearing a similar cloak.
I said:
“If you took his garment and wore it together with yours, you would have a complete outfit, and you could give him another garment.”
He replied:
There was once an argument between me and another man whose mother was non-Arab, and I insulted him through his mother.
He complained about me to the Prophet ﷺ, who said to me:
“Did you insult so-and-so?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“Did you insult him because of his mother?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
“You are a man in whom there is still some Jāhiliyyah.”
I asked:
“Even at this stage of my life, despite my old age?”
He said:
“Yes. They are your brothers whom Allah has placed under your authority. So whoever has a brother whom Allah has placed under his authority should feed him from what he himself eats, clothe him from what he himself wears, and not burden him with work that overwhelms him. If he does burden him with something overwhelming, then let him help him with it.”

١٤٠٠٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إذا صنع لأحدكم خادمه طعامه، ثم جاءه به، وقد ولي حره ودخانه، فليقعده معه فليأكل، فإن كان الطعام مشفوهًا قليلًا، فليضع في يده منه أكلة أو أكلتين)).
قال داود: ((يعني لقمة أو لقمتين)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٦٣: ٤٢).

“Did the Prophet ﷺ command that he be invited to eat?”
Jābir replied:
“Yes. If one of you dislikes having him eat alongside him, then let him at least place a portion of the food in his hand.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (198).

١٤٠٠٥ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو يقول: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، كم نعفو عن الخادم؟ فصمت، ثم أعاد عليه الكلام، فصمت، فلما كان في الثالثة قال:
((اعفوا عنه في كل يوم سبعين مرة)).

14005 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, how many times should we pardon a servant?”
He remained silent.
The man repeated the question, and he remained silent again.
When he asked a third time, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Pardon him seventy times every day.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5164), al-Tirmidhī (1949, in the second narration), and al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (3/7).

١٤٠٠٦ — عن زاذان أبي عمر قال: أتيت ابن عمر وقد أعتق مملوكًا، قال: فأخذ من الأرض عودًا أو شيئًا، فقال: ما فيه من الأجر ما يسوى هذا، إلا أني سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((من لطم مملوكه، أو ضربه، فكفارته أن يعتقه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٥٧).

14006 — Zādhān Abū ʿUmar narrated:
I came to Ibn ʿUmar after he had freed a slave.
He picked up a stick or something similar from the ground and said:
“There is not even this much reward in what I have done, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Whoever slaps his slave or strikes him, the expiation for that is to free him.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1657).

١٤٠٠٧ — عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري قال: كنت أضرب غلامًا لي، فسمعت من خلفي صوتًا:
((اعلم، أبا مسعود، للّٰه أقدر عليك منك عليه)).
فالتفت فإذا هو رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، هو حر لوجه اللّٰه. فقال:
((أما لو لم تفعل للفحتك النار)).
أو:
((لمستك النار)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٥٩: ٣٥).

14007 — Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī narrated:
I was striking a servant of mine when I heard a voice behind me saying:
“Know, O Abū Masʿūd, that Allah has more power over you than you have over him.”
I turned around and saw that it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, he is free for the sake of Allah.”
He replied:
“Had you not done so, the Fire would have scorched you,”
or:
“the Fire would have touched you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1659:35).

١٤٠٠٨ — عن هلال بن يساف قال: عجل شيخ فلطم خادمًا له، فقال له سويد بن مقرن: عجز عليك إلا حر وجهها؟ لقد رأيتني سابع سبعة من بني مقرن، ما لنا خادم إلا واحدة، لطمها أصغرنا، فأمرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن نعتقها.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٥٨: ٣٢).

14008 — Hilāl ibn Yasāf narrated:
An elderly man became hasty and slapped a female servant of his.
Suwayd ibn Muqarrin said to him:
“Could you find nothing to strike except her face? I remember when I was one of seven brothers from Banū Muqarrin, and we had only one female servant. The youngest of us slapped her, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to free her.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1658:32).

١٤٠٠٩ — عن معاوية بن سويد قال: لطمت مولى لنا فهربت، ثم جئت قبيل الظهر، فصليت خلف أبي، فدعاه ودعاني، ثم قال: امتثل منه، فعفا، ثم قال: كنا بني مقرن على عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليس لنا إلا خادم واحدة، فلطمها أحدنا، فبلغ ذلك النبي ﷺ فقال:
((أعتقوها)).
قالوا: ليس لهم خادم غيرها.
قال:
((فليستخدموها، فإذا استغنوا عنها فليخلوا سبيلها)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٥٨: ٣١).

14009 — Muʿāwiyah ibn Suwayd narrated:
I slapped a servant belonging to us and then fled.
I returned shortly before Ẓuhr and prayed behind my father.
He called the servant and called me, then said:
“Take retaliation from him.”
But the servant pardoned me.
Then my father said:
“We, Banū Muqarrin, during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only one female servant. One of us slapped her, and this reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he said:
‘Free her.’
They said:
‘They have no servant besides her.’
He said:
‘Then let them continue to employ her until they no longer need her, and when they can do without her, let them set her free.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1658:31).

١٤٠١٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت أبا القاسم ﷺ يقول:

14010 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
I heard Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ say:
“Whoever falsely accuses his slave of zinā while the slave is innocent of what he said will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection, unless the accusation was in fact true.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6858) and Muslim (1660:37).

١٤٠١٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((للعبد المملوك المصلح أجران)).
والذي نفس أبي هريرة بيده، لولا الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه، والحج، وبر أمي، لأحببت أن أموت وأنا مملوك.
قال: وبلغنا أن أبا هريرة لم يكن يحج حتى ماتت أمه لصحبتها.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٥٤٨)، ومسلم (١٦٦٥: ٤٤).

14012 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A righteous slave who fulfills his duties receives two rewards.”
Abū Hurayrah then said:
“By the One in whose hand is the soul of Abū Hurayrah, were it not for striving in the cause of Allah, performing Ḥajj, and dutifulness to my mother, I would have loved to die while being a slave.”
It was also reported to us that Abū Hurayrah would not perform Ḥajj while his mother was alive because he remained with her in service and companionship.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2548) and Muslim (1665:44).

١٤٠١٣ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((ثلاثة يؤتون أجرهم مرتين: الرجل تكون له الأمة، فيعلمها فيحسن تعليمها، ويؤدبها فيحسن أدبها، ثم يعتقها فيتزوجها فله أجران، ومؤمن أهل الكتاب، الذي كان مؤمنًا، ثم آمن بالنبي ﷺ، فله أجران، والعبد الذي يؤدي حق اللّٰه، وينصح لسيده)).
ثم قال الشعبي: وأعطيتكها بغير شيء، وقد كان الرجل يرحل في أهون منها إلى المدينة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠١١)، ومسلم (١٥٤: ٢٤١).

english_source:
14013 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Three people will be given their reward twice: a man who has a female slave, teaches her and teaches her well, disciplines and educates her well, then frees her and marries her—he has two rewards; a believer from the People of the Book who had already believed and then believed in the Prophet ﷺ—he has two rewards; and a slave who fulfills the right of Allah and is sincere to his master.”
Then al-Shaʿbī said:
“I have given this hadith to you for nothing, whereas a man used to travel to Madinah for something less important than this.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3011) and Muslim (154:241).

((نعم ما لأحدهم يحسن عبادة ربه وينصح سيده)).

١٤٠١٦ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((كلكم راع فمسؤول عن رعيته، فالأمير الذي على الناس راع عليهم وهو مسؤول عنهم، والرجل راع على أهل بيته وهو مسؤول عنهم، والمرأة راعية على بيت بعلها وولده وهي مسؤولة عنهم، والعبد راع على مال سيده وهو مسؤول عنه، ألا فكلكم راع وكلكم مسؤول عن رعيته)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٥٥٤)، ومسلم (١٨٢٩).

14016 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Every one of you is a shepherd and every one of you is responsible for those under his care. The ruler over the people is a shepherd over them and is responsible for them. A man is a shepherd over the members of his household and is responsible for them. A woman is a shepherd over the home of her husband and his children and is responsible for them. A slave is a shepherd over the property of his master and is responsible for it. Indeed, every one of you is a shepherd, and every one of you is responsible for his flock.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2554) and Muslim (1829).

١٤٠١٧ — عن عائشة قالت: ما ضرب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ شيئًا قط بيده، ولا امرأة، ولا خادمًا، إلا أن يجاهد في سبيل اللّٰه، وما نيل منه شيء قط، فينتقم من صاحبه، إلا أن ينتهك شيء من محارم اللّٰه، فينتقم للّٰه عز وجل.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣٢٨).

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2328).

١٤٠١٩ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ:
((ليس منا من خبب امرأة على زوجها، أو عبدًا على سيده)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١٧٥)، وأحمد (٩١٥٧)، وابن حبان (٥٦٨، ٥٥٦٠)، والحاكم (٢/١٩٦).
قوله: “خبب” معناه: أفسد، وخدع، وقد جاء بلفظ: “أفسد” في بعض الروايات.

14019 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“He is not of us who corrupts a woman against her husband or a slave against his master.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2175), Aḥmad (9157), Ibn Ḥibbān (568, 5560), and al-Ḥākim (2/196).
The word:
“khabbaba”
means to corrupt or deceive.
Some narrations explicitly use the wording:
“afsada” — “corrupted.”

١٤٠٢٢ — عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم، عن أبيه: أن النبي ﷺ قال في أسارى بدر:
((لو كان المطعم بن عدي حيًّا، ثم كلمني في هؤلاء النتنى لتركتهم له)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣١٣٩).
والمطعم بن عدي هو: ابن نوفل بن عبد مناف بن قصي، هو الذي قام في نقض صحيفة القطيعة، وكان يحنو على أهل الشعب، ويصلهم في السر، وهو الذي أجار النبي ﷺ حين رجع من الطائف.

14022 — Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim narrated from his father that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the captives of Badr:
“Had al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī been alive and then spoken to me concerning these foul-smelling captives, I would have released them for his sake.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3139).
Al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī was the son of Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy.
He was among those who took action to annul the boycott document. He showed compassion toward those confined in the mountain pass and secretly maintained ties with them.
He was also the one who granted protection to the Prophet ﷺ when he returned from al-Ṭāʾif.

والمطعم بن عدي هو: ابن نوفل بن عبد مناف بن قصي، هو الذي قام في نقض صحيفة القطيعة، وكان يحنو على أهل الشعب، ويصلهم في السر، وهو الذي أجار النبي ﷺ حين رجع من الطائف.
14022 — Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim narrated from his father that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the captives of Badr:
“Had al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī been alive and then spoken to me concerning these foul-smelling captives, I would have released them for his sake.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3139).
Al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī was the son of Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy.
He was among those who took action to annul the boycott document. He showed compassion toward those confined in the mountain pass and secretly maintained ties with them.
He was also the one who granted protection to the Prophet ﷺ when he returned from al-Ṭāʾif.

14023 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ mentioning one of his sons-in-law from Banū ʿAbd Shams. He praised him for the way he had conducted himself as a son-in-law and spoke well of him.
He said:
“He spoke to me and told me the truth, and he made me a promise and fulfilled it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3729) and Muslim (2449:95).
The person intended from Banū ʿAbd Shams was Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd Shams.
The Prophet ﷺ had married his eldest daughter, Zaynab, to him before the beginning of Prophethood.
Abū al-ʿĀṣ later participated in the Battle of Badr alongside the polytheists and was captured.
Zaynab paid his ransom, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stipulated that he send her to Madinah. He fulfilled that promise, so the Prophet ﷺ praised him for keeping his covenant.
Abū al-ʿĀṣ later embraced Islam shortly before the Conquest of Makkah and migrated to Madinah, whereupon the Prophet ﷺ returned his daughter to him.
It is authentically established in al-Bukhārī and Muslim that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray while carrying Umāmah, the daughter of Zaynab by Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib later married this Umāmah after the death of her maternal aunt Fāṭimah.
Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ died during the caliphate of Abū Bakr, in Dhū al-Ḥijjah of the year 12 AH.

١٤٠٢٤ — عن المستورد القرشي قال - وكان عند عمرو بن العاص -: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((تقوم الساعة، والروم أكثر الناس)).
فقال له عمرو: أبصر ما تقول.
قال: أقول ما سمعت من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
قال: لئن قلت ذلك إن فيهم لخصالًا أربعًا: إنهم لأحلم الناس عند فتنة، وأسرعهم إفاقة بعد مصيبة، وأوشكهم كرة بعد فرة، وخيرهم لمسكين ويتيم وضعيف، وخامسة حسنة جميلة: وأمنعهم من ظلم الملوك.
صحيح: رواه مسلم في الفتن (٢٨٩٨).

14024 — Al-Mustawrid al-Qurashī narrated—while he was in the presence of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“The Hour will be established while the Romans are the majority of mankind.”
ʿAmr said to him:
“Be careful about what you are saying.”
He replied:
“I am only saying what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
ʿAmr said:
“If you say that, then indeed they possess four qualities: they are the most forbearing of people at the time of tribulation, the quickest to recover after calamity, the quickest to return to battle after fleeing, and the best of people toward the poor, the orphan, and the weak.
And there is a fifth, beautiful and excellent quality: they are the people most capable of preventing the oppression of kings.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim in Kitāb al-Fitan (2898).

14025 — Al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān al-Anṣārī narrated:
I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about righteousness and sin.
He replied:
“Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers uneasily within your chest and which you dislike for people to discover.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2553).

١٤٠٢٦ — عن أبي ثعلبة الخشني يقول: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، أخبرني بما يحل لي ويحرم علي. قال: فصعد النبي ﷺ وصوب في النظر، فقال:
((البر ما سكنت إليه النفس واطمأن إليه القلب، والإثم ما لم تسكن إليه النفس ولم يطمئن إليه القلب، وإن أفتاك المفتون)).
وقال:
((لا تقرب لحم الحمار الأهلي، ولا ذا ناب من السباع)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٧٧٤٢).

14026 — Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī narrated:
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, tell me what is lawful for me and what is forbidden to me.”
The Prophet ﷺ looked me over carefully and said:
“Righteousness is that with which the soul becomes tranquil and the heart finds reassurance. Sin is that with which the soul does not become tranquil and the heart does not find reassurance, even if those who give legal verdicts give you a verdict.”
He also said:
“Do not approach the meat of domesticated donkeys, nor any predatory animal possessing fangs.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (17742).

١٤٠٢٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود قال: سألت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: أي الأعمال أحب إلى اللّٰه؟ قال:
((الصلاة على وقتها)).
قلت: ثم أي؟ قال:
((ثم بر الوالدين)).
قلت: ثم أي؟ قال:
((ثم الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه)).
قال: حدثني بهن، ولو استزدته لزادني.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٧٠)، ومسلم (٨٥: ١٣٩).

14027 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“Which deeds are most beloved to Allah?”
He replied:
“Prayer at its proper time.”
I asked:
“Then which?”
He said:
“Then dutifulness to one’s parents.”
I asked:
“Then which?”
He replied:
“Then striving in the cause of Allah.”
Ibn Masʿūd said:
“He told me these, and had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5970) and Muslim (85:139).

١٤٠٢٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((بينما ثلاثة نفر يتمشون أخذهم المطر، فمالوا إلى غار في الجبل، فانحطت على فم غارهم صخرة من الجبل فأطبقت عليهم، فقال بعضهم لبعض: انظروا أعمالًا عملتموها للّٰه صالحة، فادعوا اللّٰه بها لعله يفرجها.
فقال أحدهم: اللهم إنه كان لي والدان شيخان كبيران، ولي صبية صغار، كنت أرعى عليهم، فإذا رحت عليهم فحلبت بدأت بوالدي أسقيهما قبل ولدي، وإنه ناء بي الشجر، فما أتيت حتى أمسيت، فوجدتهما قد ناما، فحلبت كما كنت أحلب، فجئت بالحلاب، فقمت عند رؤوسهما، أكره أن أوقظهما من نومهما، وأكره أن أبدأ بالصبية قبلهما، والصبية يتضاغون عند قدمي، فلم يزل ذلك دأبي ودأبهم حتى طلع الفجر. فإن كنت تعلم أني فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج لنا فرجة نرى منها السماء. ففرج اللّٰه لهم فرجة حتى يرون منها السماء.
وقال الثاني: اللهم إنه كانت لي ابنة عم أحبها كأشد ما يحب الرجال النساء، فطلبت إليها نفسها، فأبت حتى آتيها بمائة دينار، فسعيت حتى جمعت مائة دينار، فلقيتها بها، فلما قعدت بين رجليها قالت: يا عبد اللّٰه، اتق اللّٰه، ولا تفتح الخاتم، فقمت عنها. اللهم فإن كنت تعلم أني قد فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج لنا منها. ففرج لهم فرجة.
وقال الآخر: اللهم إني كنت استأجرت أجيرًا بفرق أرز، فلما قضى عمله قال: أعطني حقي. فعرضت عليه حقه فتركه ورغب عنه، فلم أزل أزرعه حتى جمعت منه بقرًا وراعيها، فجاءني فقال: اتق اللّٰه ولا تظلمني وأعطني حقي. فقلت: اذهب إلى ذلك البقر وراعيها. فقال: اتق اللّٰه ولا تهزأ بي. فقلت: إني لا أهزأ بك، فخذ ذلك البقر وراعيها. فأخذه فانطلق بها. فإن كنت تعلم أني فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج ما بقي. ففرج اللّٰه عنهم)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٧٤)، ومسلم (٢٧٤٣)، واللفظ للبخاري.

14028 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“While three men were walking, rain overtook them, so they took shelter in a cave in a mountain. A rock fell from the mountain over the entrance of their cave and sealed them inside. They said to one another: ‘Think of righteous deeds you performed sincerely for Allah, and supplicate to Allah by means of them; perhaps He will relieve you.’”
One of them said:
“O Allah, I had two elderly parents and small children for whom I used to graze livestock. When I returned in the evening and milked the animals, I would begin with my parents and give them milk before my children. One day, the grazing took me far away, and I did not return until evening. I found that they had fallen asleep. I milked as I normally did and brought the vessel, then stood by their heads, disliking to wake them from their sleep and also disliking to give my children before them. Meanwhile, the children were crying from hunger at my feet. This remained my condition and theirs until dawn. O Allah, if You know that I did this seeking Your Face alone, then make an opening for us through which we can see the sky.”
Allah opened a gap for them until they could see the sky.
The second man said:
“O Allah, I had a female cousin whom I loved as intensely as a man can love a woman. I sought to have relations with her, but she refused unless I brought her one hundred dinars. I worked until I had gathered one hundred dinars and then came to her with it. When I sat between her legs, she said: ‘O servant of Allah, fear Allah and do not break the seal unlawfully.’ So I got up and left her. O Allah, if You know that I did that seeking Your Face, then open a way for us.”
So Allah opened another gap for them.
The third said:
“O Allah, I once hired a laborer for a faraq of rice. When he completed his work, he said: ‘Give me my wage.’ I offered him what was due to him, but he left it and turned away from it. I continued cultivating and investing it until from it I accumulated cattle and their herdsman. Later he came and said: ‘Fear Allah, do not wrong me, and give me my right.’ I said: ‘Go to those cattle and their herdsman.’ He replied: ‘Fear Allah and do not mock me.’ I said: ‘I am not mocking you. Take those cattle and their herdsman.’ So he took them and went away with them. O Allah, if You know that I did that seeking Your Face, then remove what remains.”
Then Allah released them completely.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5974) and Muslim (2743). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

“While three men were walking, rain overtook them, so they took shelter in a cave in a mountain. A rock fell from the mountain over the entrance of their cave and sealed them inside. They said to one another: ‘Think of righteous deeds you performed sincerely for Allah, and supplicate to Allah by means of them; perhaps He will relieve you.’”
One of them said:
“O Allah, I had two elderly parents and small children for whom I used to graze livestock. When I returned in the evening and milked the animals, I would begin with my parents and give them milk before my children. One day, the grazing took me far away, and I did not return until evening. I found that they had fallen asleep. I milked as I normally did and brought the vessel, then stood by their heads, disliking to wake them from their sleep and also disliking to give my children before them. Meanwhile, the children were crying from hunger at my feet. This remained my condition and theirs until dawn. O Allah, if You know that I did this seeking Your Face alone, then make an opening for us through which we can see the sky.”
Allah opened a gap for them until they could see the sky.
The second man said:
“O Allah, I had a female cousin whom I loved as intensely as a man can love a woman. I sought to have relations with her, but she refused unless I brought her one hundred dinars. I worked until I had gathered one hundred dinars and then came to her with it. When I sat between her legs, she said: ‘O servant of Allah, fear Allah and do not break the seal unlawfully.’ So I got up and left her. O Allah, if You know that I did that seeking Your Face, then open a way for us.”
So Allah opened another gap for them.
The third said:
“O Allah, I once hired a laborer for a faraq of rice. When he completed his work, he said: ‘Give me my wage.’ I offered him what was due to him, but he left it and turned away from it. I continued cultivating and investing it until from it I accumulated cattle and their herdsman. Later he came and said: ‘Fear Allah, do not wrong me, and give me my right.’ I said: ‘Go to those cattle and their herdsman.’ He replied: ‘Fear Allah and do not mock me.’ I said: ‘I am not mocking you. Take those cattle and their herdsman.’ So he took them and went away with them. O Allah, if You know that I did that seeking Your Face, then remove what remains.”
Then Allah released them completely.

١٤٠٢٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((بينما ثلاثة نفر يتمشون أخذهم المطر، فمالوا إلى غار في الجبل، فانحطت على فم غارهم صخرة من الجبل فأطبقت عليهم، فقال بعضهم لبعض: انظروا أعمالًا عملتموها للّٰه صالحة، فادعوا اللّٰه بها لعله يفرجها.
فقال أحدهم: اللهم إنه كان لي والدان شيخان كبيران، ولي صبية صغار، كنت أرعى عليهم، فإذا رحت عليهم فحلبت بدأت بوالدي أسقيهما قبل ولدي، وإنه ناء بي الشجر، فما أتيت حتى أمسيت، فوجدتهما قد ناما، فحلبت كما كنت أحلب، فجئت بالحلاب، فقمت عند رؤوسهما، أكره أن أوقظهما من نومهما، وأكره أن أبدأ بالصبية قبلهما، والصبية يتضاغون عند قدمي، فلم يزل ذلك دأبي ودأبهم حتى طلع الفجر. فإن كنت تعلم أني فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج لنا فرجة نرى منها السماء. ففرج اللّٰه لهم فرجة حتى يرون منها السماء.
وقال الثاني: اللهم إنه كانت لي ابنة عم أحبها كأشد ما يحب الرجال النساء، فطلبت إليها نفسها، فأبت حتى آتيها بمائة دينار، فسعيت حتى جمعت مائة دينار، فلقيتها بها، فلما قعدت بين رجليها قالت: يا عبد اللّٰه، اتق اللّٰه، ولا تفتح الخاتم، فقمت عنها. اللهم فإن كنت تعلم أني قد فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج لنا منها. ففرج لهم فرجة.
وقال الآخر: اللهم إني كنت استأجرت أجيرًا بفرق أرز، فلما قضى عمله قال: أعطني حقي. فعرضت عليه حقه فتركه ورغب عنه، فلم أزل أزرعه حتى جمعت منه بقرًا وراعيها، فجاءني فقال: اتق اللّٰه ولا تظلمني وأعطني حقي. فقلت: اذهب إلى ذلك البقر وراعيها. فقال: اتق اللّٰه ولا تهزأ بي. فقلت: إني لا أهزأ بك، فخذ ذلك البقر وراعيها. فأخذه فانطلق بها. فإن كنت تعلم أني فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك فافرج ما بقي. ففرج اللّٰه عنهم)).

14029 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A child can never fully repay his father except if he finds him enslaved, purchases him, and then frees him.”
In another wording:
“A child cannot fully repay his father.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1510).

١٤٠٣٠ — عن أبي الدرداء أن رجلًا أتاه فقال: إن لي امرأة، وإن أمي تأمرني بطلاقها. قال أبو الدرداء: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((الوالد أوسط أبواب الجنة، فإن شئت فأضع ذلك الباب أو احفظه)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٩٠٠)، وأحمد (٢٧٥١١)، والحاكم (٤/١٥٢).

14030 — Abū al-Dardāʾ narrated:
A man came to him and said:
“I have a wife, and my mother is ordering me to divorce her.”
Abū al-Dardāʾ replied:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“The father is the middle—and best—of the gates of Paradise. So if you wish, neglect that gate, or preserve it.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (1900), Aḥmad (27511), and al-Ḥākim (4/152).

14031 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, who among people has the greatest right to my good companionship?”
He replied:
“Your mother.”
The man asked:
“Then who?”
He replied:
“Then your mother.”
He asked:
“Then who?”
He replied:
“Then your mother.”
He asked:
“Then who?”
He replied:
“Then your father.”
In another narration:
“Then the nearest to you, and then the next nearest.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5971) and Muslim (2548:1). The second wording was also narrated by Muslim (2548).

14032 — Bahz ibn Ḥakīm narrated from his father, from his grandfather:
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I show the greatest dutifulness?”
He replied:
“Your mother.”
I asked:
“Then whom?”
He said:
“Your mother.”
I asked:
“Then whom?”
He said:
“Your mother.”
I asked:
“Then whom?”
He replied:
“Then your father, then the closest relative, followed by the next closest.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5139), al-Tirmidhī (1897), Aḥmad (20028), and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad.

“Then whom?”

“Indeed, Allah commands you concerning your fathers. Indeed, Allah commands you concerning the nearest relative, then the next nearest.”

١٤٠٣٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((لم يتكلم في المهد إلا ثلاثة: عيسى ابن مريم، وصاحب جريج. وكان جريج رجلًا عابدًا، فاتخذ صومعة، فكان فيها، فأتته أمه وهو يصلي، فقالت: يا جريج. فقال: يا رب، أمي وصلاتي. فأقبل على صلاته، فانصرفت. فلما كان من الغد أتته وهو يصلي، فقالت: يا جريج. فقال: يا رب، أمي وصلاتي. فأقبل على صلاته، فانصرفت. فلما كان من الغد أتته وهو يصلي، فقالت: يا جريج. فقال: أي رب، أمي وصلاتي. فأقبل على صلاته، فقالت: اللهم لا تمته حتى ينظر إلى وجوه المومسات.
فتذاكر بنو إسرائيل جريجًا وعبادته، وكانت امرأة بغي يتمثل بحسنها، فقالت: إن شئتم لأفتننه لكم. قال: فتعرضت له، فلم يلتفت إليها، فأتت راعيًا كان يأوي إلى صومعته، فأمكنته من نفسها، فوقع عليها فحملت، فلما ولدت قالت: هو من جريج. فأتوه فاستنزلوه، وهدموا صومعته، وجعلوا يضربونه. فقال: ما شأنكم؟ قالوا: زنيت بهذه البغي، فولدت منك. فقال: أين الصبي؟ فجاءوا به. فقال: دعوني حتى أصلي. فصلى، فلما انصرف أتى الصبي فطعن في بطنه، وقال: يا غلام، من أبوك؟ قال: فلان الراعي.
قال: فأقبلوا على جريج يقبلونه ويتمسحون به، وقالوا: نبني لك صومعتك من ذهب. قال: لا، أعيدوها من طين كما كانت. ففعلوا)). الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٣٦)، ومسلم (٢٥٥٠: ٨).
وقوله: “المومسات” بضم الميم الأولى، وكسر الثانية، أي: الزواني البغايا المتجاهرات.
وقوله: “يتمثل بحسنها” أي: يضرب به المثل لانفرادها.
فائدة: كان في شريعة جريج إجابة الأم في الصلوات، فلما لم يجب جريج أمه أصابه دعاؤها عليه.
وأما في الإسلام فلا تجب إجابة الأم في الصلوات المفروضة.
وأما النوافل فاختلف أهل العلم فيه، ومن أصح الأقوال أن الأفضل أن يجيب، ثم يعود إلى صلاته ويكملها.

14035 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Only three spoke while still in the cradle: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and the child connected with the story of Jurayj…”
Jurayj was a devoted worshipper who had built himself a hermitage and remained there.
His mother came to him while he was praying and called:
“O Jurayj!”
He said to himself:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He chose to continue his prayer, so she left.
The next day she came again while he was praying and called:
“O Jurayj!”
He said:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He continued his prayer, and she left.
The following day she came while he was praying and called him again:
“O Jurayj!”
He said:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He continued his prayer.
She then said:
“O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of prostitutes.”
The Children of Israel began discussing Jurayj and his worship.
There was a prostitute whose beauty was proverbial. She said:
“If you wish, I will tempt him for you.”
She presented herself to him, but he paid no attention to her.
She then went to a shepherd who used to seek shelter near Jurayj’s hermitage and offered herself to him. He had intercourse with her and she became pregnant.
When she gave birth, she said:
“The child belongs to Jurayj.”
The people came to Jurayj, forced him down from his hermitage, demolished it, and began beating him.
He asked:
“What is wrong with you?”
They replied:
“You committed zinā with this prostitute, and she has given birth to your child.”
He asked:
“Where is the child?”
They brought the infant.
Jurayj said:
“Leave me until I pray.”
He prayed, then came to the child, poked him in the stomach, and asked:
“O boy, who is your father?”
The infant replied:
“So-and-so, the shepherd.”
The people then turned toward Jurayj, kissing him and touching him seeking blessing, and said:
“We will rebuild your hermitage out of gold.”
He replied:
“No. Rebuild it from clay just as it was.”
So they did.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3436) and Muslim (2550:8).
The word “al-mūmisāt,” with a ḍammah on the first mīm and a kasrah on the second, means openly practicing prostitutes and adulteresses.
The words “yutamaththalu bi-ḥusnihā” mean that her beauty was proverbial because of how exceptional it was.
Benefit: In the religious law applicable to Jurayj, responding to one’s mother during prayer was required. When Jurayj failed to answer his mother, her supplication against him affected him.
As for Islam, responding to one’s mother is not required while performing an obligatory prayer.
As for voluntary prayers, the scholars differed. One of the strongest opinions is that it is preferable for him to answer her and then return to his prayer and complete it.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٣٦)، ومسلم (٢٥٥٠: ٨).
وقوله: “المومسات” بضم الميم الأولى، وكسر الثانية، أي: الزواني البغايا المتجاهرات.
وقوله: “يتمثل بحسنها” أي: يضرب به المثل لانفرادها.
فائدة: كان في شريعة جريج إجابة الأم في الصلوات، فلما لم يجب جريج أمه أصابه دعاؤها عليه.
وأما في الإسلام فلا تجب إجابة الأم في الصلوات المفروضة.
وأما النوافل فاختلف أهل العلم فيه، ومن أصح الأقوال أن الأفضل أن يجيب، ثم يعود إلى صلاته ويكملها.
14035 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Only three spoke while still in the cradle: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and the child connected with the story of Jurayj…”
Jurayj was a devoted worshipper who had built himself a hermitage and remained there.
His mother came to him while he was praying and called:
“O Jurayj!”
He said to himself:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He chose to continue his prayer, so she left.
The next day she came again while he was praying and called:
“O Jurayj!”
He said:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He continued his prayer, and she left.
The following day she came while he was praying and called him again:
“O Jurayj!”
He said:
“My Lord, my mother or my prayer?”
He continued his prayer.
She then said:
“O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of prostitutes.”
The Children of Israel began discussing Jurayj and his worship.
There was a prostitute whose beauty was proverbial. She said:
“If you wish, I will tempt him for you.”
She presented herself to him, but he paid no attention to her.
She then went to a shepherd who used to seek shelter near Jurayj’s hermitage and offered herself to him. He had intercourse with her and she became pregnant.
When she gave birth, she said:
“The child belongs to Jurayj.”
The people came to Jurayj, forced him down from his hermitage, demolished it, and began beating him.
He asked:
“What is wrong with you?”
They replied:
“You committed zinā with this prostitute, and she has given birth to your child.”
He asked:
“Where is the child?”
They brought the infant.
Jurayj said:
“Leave me until I pray.”
He prayed, then came to the child, poked him in the stomach, and asked:
“O boy, who is your father?”
The infant replied:
“So-and-so, the shepherd.”
The people then turned toward Jurayj, kissing him and touching him seeking blessing, and said:
“We will rebuild your hermitage out of gold.”
He replied:
“No. Rebuild it from clay just as it was.”
So they did.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3436) and Muslim (2550:8).
The word “al-mūmisāt,” with a ḍammah on the first mīm and a kasrah on the second, means openly practicing prostitutes and adulteresses.
The words “yutamaththalu bi-ḥusnihā” mean that her beauty was proverbial because of how exceptional it was.
Benefit: In the religious law applicable to Jurayj, responding to one’s mother during prayer was required. When Jurayj failed to answer his mother, her supplication against him affected him.
As for Islam, responding to one’s mother is not required while performing an obligatory prayer.
As for voluntary prayers, the scholars differed. One of the strongest opinions is that it is preferable for him to answer her and then return to his prayer and complete it.

١٤٠٣٦ — عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت: قدمت علي أمي وهي مشركة في عهد قريش إذ عاهدهم، فاستفتيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، قدمت علي أمي وهي راغبة، أفأصل أمي؟ قال:
((نعم، صلي أمك)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٢٠)، ومسلم (١٠٠٣).
ورواه البخاري (٥٩٧٨) وزاد: فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى فيها: ﴿لَا يَنْهَاكُمُ اللّٰهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوا إِلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللّٰهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [الممتحنة: ٨].

14036 — Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr narrated:
My mother came to me while she was still a polytheist, during the period in which Quraysh had a treaty with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
So I sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, my mother has come to me desiring good relations. Should I maintain ties with my mother?”
He replied:
“Yes, maintain ties with your mother.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2620) and Muslim (1003).
Al-Bukhārī (5978) also narrated it and added that Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning her:
“Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and justly with those who did not fight you because of religion and did not expel you from your homes. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.”
 [Sūrat al-Mumtaḥanah 60:8]

١٤٠٣٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: مر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على عبد اللّٰه بن أبي ابن سلول، وحوله نفر من قومه، فقال: قد غبر علينا ابن أبي كبشة. فقال عبد اللّٰه بن عبد اللّٰه: والذي أكرمك، والذي أنزل عليك الكتاب، لئن شئت لأتيتك برأسه. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لا، ولكن بر أباك، وأحسن صحبته)).
حسن: رواه ابن حبان في صحيحه (٤٢٨)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (٢٧٠٨).

14037 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl while a group of his people were around him.
He said:
“Ibn Abī Kabshah has stirred up trouble for us.”
Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
“By the One who honored you and sent down the Book to you, if you wish, I will bring you his head.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“No. Rather, be dutiful to your father and keep good companionship with him.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (428) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2708).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl while a group of his people were around him.
He said:
“Ibn Abī Kabshah has stirred up trouble for us.”
Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
“By the One who honored you and sent down the Book to you, if you wish, I will bring you his head.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“No. Rather, be dutiful to your father and keep good companionship with him.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (428) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2708).

“Whoever lives to see his parents, or one of them, and then still enters the Fire afterward, may Allah cast him far away and remove him from His mercy.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (19027), al-Ṭayālisī (1418), and al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (2/40).

((إن اللّٰه حرم عليكم عقوق الأمهات، ووأد البنات، ومنعًا وهات، وكره لكم ثلاثًا: قيل وقال، وكثرة السؤال، وإضاعة المال)).

14040 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah has forbidden you from disobedience to mothers, burying daughters alive, withholding what is due while continually asking from others, and He dislikes for you three things: gossiping about what was said, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2408) and Muslim (593, following 1715).

١٤٠٤١ — عن أبي بكرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ألا أنبئكم بأكبر الكبائر؟)).
قلنا: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه.
قال:
((الإشراك باللّٰه، وعقوق الوالدين)).
وكان متكئًا فجلس فقال:
((ألا وقول الزور، وشهادة الزور، ألا وقول الزور، وشهادة الزور)).
فما زال يقولها، حتى قلت: لا يسكت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٧٦)، ومسلم (٨٧).

14041 — Abū Bakrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Shall I inform you of the greatest of the major sins?”
We replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Associating partners with Allah and disobedience to parents.”
He had been reclining, then he sat up and said:
“And beware of false speech and false testimony! Beware of false speech and false testimony!”
He continued repeating it until I thought:
“He will not stop.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5976) and Muslim (87).

١٤٠٤٢ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: ذكر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الكبائر، أو سئل عن الكبائر، فقال:
((الشرك باللّٰه، وقتل النفس، وعقوق الوالدين)).
وقال:
((ألا أنبئكم بأكبر الكبائر؟)).
قال:

أو قال:
((شهادة الزور)).
قال شعبة: وأكثر ظني أنه قال: ((شهادة الزور)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٧٧)، ومسلم (٨٨: ١٤٤).

14042 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the major sins—or was asked about the major sins—and said:
“Associating partners with Allah, unlawfully killing a soul, and disobedience to parents.”
Then he said:
“Shall I inform you of the greatest of the major sins?”
He said:
“False speech,”
or:
“False testimony.”
Shuʿbah said:
“I strongly think that he said: ‘false testimony.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5977) and Muslim (88:144).

١٤٠٤٣ — عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ثلاثة لا ينظر اللّٰه عز وجل إليهم يوم القيامة: العاق لوالديه، والمرأة المترجلة، والديوث، وثلاثة لا يدخلون الجنة: العاق لوالديه، والمدمن على الخمر، والمنان بما أعطى)).
حسن: رواه النسائي (٢٥٦٢).
وقوله: “الديوث” بتشديد الياء هو الذي يقر أهله على الزنا مع علمه.

14043 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There are three whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not look at on the Day of Resurrection: one who is disobedient to his parents, a woman who imitates men, and a dayyūth. And there are three who will not enter Paradise: one who is disobedient to his parents, one who is addicted to intoxicants, and one who reminds people of what he has given them.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (2562).
The word “dayyūth,” with a doubled yāʾ, refers to a man who knowingly tolerates sexual immorality among the women of his household.

((ثلاثة لا ينظر اللّٰه عز وجل إليهم يوم القيامة: العاق لوالديه، والمرأة المترجلة، والديوث، وثلاثة لا يدخلون الجنة: العاق لوالديه، والمدمن على الخمر، والمنان بما أعطى)).
حسن: رواه النسائي (٢٥٦٢).
وقوله: “الديوث” بتشديد الياء هو الذي يقر أهله على الزنا مع علمه.
14043 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There are three whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not look at on the Day of Resurrection: one who is disobedient to his parents, a woman who imitates men, and a dayyūth. And there are three who will not enter Paradise: one who is disobedient to his parents, one who is addicted to intoxicants, and one who reminds people of what he has given them.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (2562).
The word “dayyūth,” with a doubled yāʾ, refers to a man who knowingly tolerates sexual immorality among the women of his household.

١٤٠٤٤ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن أنيس الجهني قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن من أكبر الكبائر: الشرك باللّٰه، وعقوق الوالدين، واليمين الغموس، وما حلف حالف باللّٰه يمين صبر، فأدخل فيها مثل جناح بعوضة إلا جعلت نكتة في قلبه إلى يوم القيامة)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٠٢٠)، وأحمد (١٦٠٤٣)، والطحاوي في شرح المشكل (٨٩٣).

14044 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Unays al-Juhanī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and the deliberately false oath. No person swears a binding oath by Allah and inserts into it even something as small as a mosquito’s wing of falsehood except that a dark mark is placed in his heart until the Day of Resurrection.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3020), Aḥmad (16043), and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ al-Mushkil (893).

١٤٠٤٥ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن من أكبر الكبائر أن يلعن الرجل والديه)).
قيل: يا رسول اللّٰه، وكيف يلعن الرجل والديه؟
قال:
((يسب الرجل أبا الرجل، فيسب أباه، ويسب أمه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٧٣)، ومسلم (٩٠)، واللفظ للبخاري.

14045 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the greatest of the major sins is for a man to curse his own parents.”
It was asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how could a man curse his own parents?”
He replied:
“He insults another man’s father, so that man insults his father; and he insults the other man’s mother, so that man insults his mother.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5973) and Muslim (90). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٤٠٤٦ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((إن أبر البر صلة الولد أهل ود أبيه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٥٢: ١١) بسنده عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر، أن رجلًا من الأعراب لقيه بطريق مكة، فسلم عليه عبد اللّٰه، وحمله على حمار كان يركبه، وأعطاه عمامة كانت على رأسه، فقال ابن دينار: فقلنا له: أصلحك اللّٰه، إنهم الأعراب، وإنهم يرضون باليسير. فقال عبد اللّٰه: إن أبا هذا كان ودًا لعمر بن الخطاب، وإني سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: فذكره.

14046 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Indeed, among the highest forms of dutifulness is for a child to maintain ties with those whom his father loved.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2552:11).
In its chain, it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar that a Bedouin man met him on the road to Makkah. ʿAbdullāh greeted him with salām, gave him the donkey that he himself had been riding, and gave him the turban that was upon his head.
Ibn Dīnār said:
We said to him:
“May Allah rectify you. They are only Bedouins, and they are satisfied with little.”
ʿAbdullāh replied:
“The father of this man was a beloved friend of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say…”
Then he mentioned the hadith above.

١٤٠٤٧ — عن أبي بردة قال: أتيت المدينة فأتاني عبد اللّٰه بن عمر فقال: هل تدري لم أتيتك؟ قال: قلت: لا. قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((من أحب أن يصل أباه في قبره فليصل إخوان أبيه بعده)).
وإنه كان بين أبي - عمر - وبين أبيك إخاء وود، فأحببت أن أصل ذلك.
صحيح: رواه أبو يعلى (٥٦٦٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٣٢).

14047 — Abū Burdah narrated:
I came to Madinah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar came to me and asked:
“Do you know why I came to you?”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Whoever wishes to maintain dutiful ties with his father after his father is in the grave should maintain ties with his father’s brothers and close friends after him.”
Then he said:
“There was brotherhood and affection between my father, ʿUmar, and your father, so I wished to maintain that bond.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (5669) and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (432).

“There was brotherhood and affection between my father, ʿUmar, and your father, so I wished to maintain that bond.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (5669) and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (432).

((فهلا عدلت بينهما)).
حسن: رواه الطحاوي في شرح معاني الآثار (٤/٨٩)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٨٣٢٧، ١٠٥١٠).

١٤٠٥٠ — عن ابن عمر أن رجلًا أتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إني أصبت ذنبًا عظيمًا، فهل لي من توبة؟ قال:
((هل لك من أم؟)).
قال: لا.
قال:
((هل لك من خالة؟)).
قال: نعم.
قال:
((فبرها)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٩٠٤)، وأحمد (٤٦٢٤)، وابن حبان (٤٣٥)، والحاكم (٤/١٥٥).
ومعنى الحديث: بعد أن تتوب إلى اللّٰه قم ببر خالتك لتكون توبتك أكثر قبولًا.

14050 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a grave sin. Is there any repentance for me?”
He asked:
“Do you have a mother?”
The man replied:
“No.”
He asked:
“Do you have a maternal aunt?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Then be dutiful to her.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (1904), Aḥmad (4624), Ibn Ḥibbān (435), and al-Ḥākim (4/155).
The meaning of the hadith is: after repenting to Allah, be dutiful toward your maternal aunt so that your repentance may be more readily accepted.

١٤٠٥١ — عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري أن رجلًا قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، أخبرني بعمل يدخلني الجنة. فقال القوم: ما له؟ ما له؟ فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أرب ما له)).
فقال النبي ﷺ:
((تعبد اللّٰه لا تشرك به شيئًا، وتقيم الصلاة، وتؤتي الزكاة، وتصل الرحم، ذرها)).
قال: كأنه كان على راحلته.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٨٣)، ومسلم (١٣: ١٣).

14051 — Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated:
A man said:
“O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me into Paradise.”
The people said:
“What is wrong with him? What is wrong with him?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“He has an important need.”
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give zakāh, and maintain the ties of kinship. Let go of it.”
The narrator said:
“It was as though the man was holding onto the Prophet’s riding animal.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5983) and Muslim (13:13).

14053 — Abū Bakrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The act of obedience whose reward comes most quickly is maintaining the ties of kinship. A household may even be sinful, yet their wealth increases and their numbers multiply when they maintain ties with one another. No household maintains kinship ties and remains in need.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (440).

١٤٠٥٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن أعجل الطاعة ثوابًا صلة الرحم، وإن أهل البيت ليكونون فجارًا فتنمو أموالهم ويكثر عددهم إذا وصلوا أرحامهم، وإن أعجل المعصية عقوبة البغي والخيانة، واليمين الغموس تذهب المال، وتقل في الرحم، وتذر الديار بلاقع)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط - مجمع البحرين (٢١٠٨).
قوله: “بلاقع” جمع بلقع وبلقعة، وهي: الأرض القفر التي لا شيء بها.

english_source:
14054 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The act of obedience whose reward comes most quickly is maintaining kinship ties. A household may be sinful, yet their wealth increases and their numbers multiply when they maintain their kinship ties. And the sins whose punishment comes most quickly are transgression and betrayal. A deliberately false oath destroys wealth, diminishes family ties, and leaves homes desolate and barren.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, as cited in Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (2108).
The word “balāqiʿ” is the plural of balqaʿ or balqaʿah, meaning barren land in which nothing remains.

١٤٠٥٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن الرحم شجنة من الرحمن، فقال اللّٰه: من وصلك وصلتُه، ومن قطعك قطعتُه)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٩٨٨).

14055 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Indeed, the bond of kinship is a branch connected to al-Raḥmān. Allah says to it: ‘Whoever maintains you, I will maintain My connection with him; and whoever severs you, I will sever him.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5988).

١٤٠٥٦ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن اللّٰه خلق الخلق، حتى إذا فرغ منهم قامت الرحم، فقالت: هذا مقام العائذ من القطيعة. قال: نعم، أما ترضين أن أصل من وصلك، وأقطع من قطعك؟ قالت: بلى. قال: فذاك لك)).
ثم قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اقرؤوا إن شئتم: ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ ۝ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللّٰهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وَأَعْمَى أَبْصَارَهُمْ ۝ أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلَى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَا﴾ [سورة محمد: ٢٢-٢٤])).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٨٧)، ومسلم (٢٥٥٤).

14056 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah created creation, and when He had finished creating them, the bond of kinship stood and said: ‘This is the place of one seeking refuge from being severed.’ Allah said: ‘Yes. Would you not be pleased that I maintain My connection with whoever maintains you, and sever whoever severs you?’ It replied: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then that is granted to you.’”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Recite, if you wish:
‘Would you then, if you were given authority, spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their sight. Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts?’”
 [Sūrat Muḥammad 47:22–24]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5987) and Muslim (2554).

١٤٠٥٧ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((الرحم معلقة بالعرش تقول: من وصلني وصله اللّٰه، ومن قطعني قطعه اللّٰه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٨٩)، ومسلم (٢٥٥٥) - واللفظ له.

14057 — ʿĀʾishah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The bond of kinship is suspended from the Throne, saying: ‘Whoever maintains me, Allah will maintain His connection with him; and whoever severs me, Allah will sever him.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5989) and Muslim (2555). The wording is that of Muslim.

١٤٠٥٨ — عن ابن عباس، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن الرحم شجنة آخذة بحجزة الرحمن، يصل من وصلها، ويقطع من قطعها)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٩٥٣)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (١٨٨٣)، والطبراني (١٠/٣٩٨).

14058 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Indeed, the bond of kinship is a branch that clings to the waist-wrapper of al-Raḥmān. He maintains His connection with whoever maintains it and severs whoever severs it.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (2953), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1883), and al-Ṭabarānī (10/398).

١٤٠٦٠ — عن عمرو بن العاص قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ جهارًا غير سر يقول:
((ألا إن آل أبي فلان - يعني فلانًا - ليسوا لي بأولياء، إنما وليي اللّٰه وصالح المؤمنين)).
وفي رواية البخاري:
((ولكن لهم رحم أبلها ببلالها)).
يعني: أصلها بصلتها.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٩٠)، ومسلم (٢١٥).

14060 — ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say openly and not secretly:
“Indeed, the family of so-and-so are not my close allies. My true Protector is Allah and the righteous believers.”
In al-Bukhārī’s narration, he added:
“However, I do have ties of kinship with them, and I will keep those ties properly maintained.”
Meaning: I will maintain those family ties through the connection due to them.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5990) and Muslim (215).

((لئن كنت كما قلت، فكأنما تُسِفُّهم الملَّ، ولا يزال معك من اللّٰه ظهير عليهم ما دمت على ذلك)).

14066 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
A man said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives whose ties I maintain, but they sever ties with me. I treat them well, but they treat me badly. I remain forbearing toward them, while they behave ignorantly toward me.”
He replied:
“If you are as you say, it is as though you are feeding them hot ashes, and you will continue to have a supporter from Allah against them for as long as you remain upon that.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2558).
The expression “tusiffuhum,” with a ḍammah on its first letter, a kasrah on the sīn, and a doubled fāʾ, is derived from saffa yasuffu. Its meaning here is that their faces are made like the color of ashes.
The word “al-mall,” with a fatḥah on the mīm, means ashes.

“The one who truly maintains kinship is not merely the one who reciprocates. Rather, the true maintainer of kinship is the one who, when his relatives sever ties with him, continues to maintain ties with them.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5991).

١٤٠٦٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر أن عمر بن الخطاب رأى حلة سيراء تباع عند باب المسجد، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، لو اشتريت هذه الحلة فلبستها يوم الجمعة، وللوفد إذا قدموا عليك؟ فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إنما يلبس هذه من لا خلاق له في الآخرة)).
ثم جاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ منها حلل، فأعطى عمر بن الخطاب منها حلة، فقال عمر: يا رسول اللّٰه، أكسوتنيها وقد قلت في حلة عطارد ما قلت؟ فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لم أكسكها لتلبسها)).
فكساها عمر أخًا له مشركًا بمكة.
وفي رواية للبخاري:
((إني لم أعطكها لتلبسها، ولكن تبيعها أو تكسوها)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في اللباس (١٨)، والبخاري (٨٨٦)، ومسلم (٢٠٦٨).

14068 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw a striped silk garment being sold near the door of the mosque and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, why not buy this garment and wear it on Fridays and when delegations come to you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Only one who has no share in the Hereafter wears this.”
Later, some garments of that type came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave one of them to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
ʿUmar said:
“O Messenger of Allah, you have clothed me with this even though you said what you said concerning the garment of ʿUṭārid?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“I did not give it to you so that you would wear it.”
So ʿUmar gave it to a polytheist brother of his in Makkah.
In al-Bukhārī’s narration:
“I did not give it to you so that you would wear it; rather, you may sell it or give it to someone else to wear.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in al-Libās (18), al-Bukhārī (886), and Muslim (2068).

١٤٠٦٩ — عن حكيم بن حزام أنه قال لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ: أي رسول اللّٰه، أرأيت أمورًا كنت أتحنث بها في الجاهلية، من صدقة، أو عتاقة، أو صلة رحم، أفيها أجر؟ فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أسلمت على ما أسلفت من خير)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٩٩٢)، ومسلم (١٢٣: ١٩٥).

14069 — Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about the acts of devotion I used to perform during the Jāhiliyyah, such as giving charity, freeing slaves, and maintaining kinship ties? Is there any reward for them?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“You embraced Islam together with the good that you had already done.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5992) and Muslim (123:195).

14071 — Saʿīd ibn Zayd narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The bond of kinship is a branch connected to al-Raḥmān. Whoever severs it, Allah forbids Paradise to him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (1651), al-Bazzār (1265), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (4/157).
The words:
“Allah forbids Paradise to him”
mean that he is forbidden from entering it initially; afterward Allah may admit him into Paradise if he is among the people of tawḥīd.

١٤٠٧٣ — عن أبي هريرة رفعه قال:
((تعرض الأعمال في كل يوم خميس واثنين، فيغفر اللّٰه عز وجل في ذلك اليوم لكل امرئ لا يشرك باللّٰه شيئًا، إلا امرأ كانت بينه وبين أخيه شحناء، فيقال: اركوا هذين حتى يصطلحا، اركوا هذين حتى يصطلحا)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٦٥: ٣٦).
قوله: “اركوا” أي: أخروا، يقال: ركاه يركوه إذا أخره.

14073 — Abū Hurayrah narrated, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ:
“Deeds are presented every Monday and Thursday. On that day Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives every person who does not associate anything with Allah, except a person between whom and his brother there is hostility. It is said: ‘Delay these two until they reconcile. Delay these two until they reconcile.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2565:36).
The word “irkū” means: “Delay them.” It is said rakāhu yarkūhu when one postpones or delays something.

((ما من ذنب أجدر أن يعجل اللّٰه لصاحبه العقوبة في الدنيا، مع ما يدخر له في الآخرة، من البغي وقطيعة الرحم)).

“There is no sin more deserving that Allah hasten its punishment for its perpetrator in this world, while also storing punishment for him in the Hereafter, than transgression and severing ties of kinship.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4902), al-Tirmidhī (2679), Ibn Mājah (4211), and Aḥmad (20374).

١٤٠٧٦ — عن عائشة قالت: دخلت امرأة معها ابنتان لها تسأل، فلم تجد عندي شيئًا غير تمرة، فأعطيتها إياها، فقسمتها بين ابنتيها، ولم تأكل منها، ثم قامت فخرجت، فدخل النبي ﷺ علينا، فأخبرته فقال:
((من ابتلي من هذه البنات بشيء كن له سترًا من النار)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٤١٨)، ومسلم (٢٦٢٩).

14076 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
A woman entered upon me accompanied by her two daughters, asking for something.
I had nothing with me except a single date, so I gave it to her.
She divided it between her two daughters and did not eat any of it herself.

14078 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No man has two daughters who reach an age at which he cares for them, and then treats them well for as long as they remain with him, except that they will cause him to enter Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (3670), Aḥmad (2104), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (77), and Ibn Ḥibbān (2945).

14082 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever supports three daughters, provides sufficiently for them, shows them mercy, and treats them gently will be in Paradise.”
A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about two?”
He replied:
“And two.”
We thought that if someone had asked:
“And one?”
he would have said:
“And one.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (2210), and this is his wording, and Ibn Abī Shaybah (943).

فقال رجل: يا رسول اللّٰه، واثنتين؟
قال:
((واثنتين)).
حتى قلنا: إن إنسانًا لو قال: واحدة، لقال: واحدة.
صحيح: رواه أبو يعلى (٢٢١٠) - والسياق له -، وابن أبي شيبة (٩٤٣).
14082 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever supports three daughters, provides sufficiently for them, shows them mercy, and treats them gently will be in Paradise.”
A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about two?”
He replied:
“And two.”
We thought that if someone had asked:
“And one?”
he would have said:
“And one.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (2210), and this is his wording, and Ibn Abī Shaybah (943).

١٤٠٨٤ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود قال: سألت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: أي الذنب أعظم عند اللّٰه؟ قال:
((أن تجعل للّٰه ندًا وهو خلقك)).
قال: قلت له: إن ذلك لعظيم. قال: قلت: ثم أي؟ قال:
((ثم أن تقتل ولدك مخافة أن يطعم معك)).
قال: قلت: ثم أي؟ قال:
((ثم أن تزاني حليلة جارك)).
زاد في رواية: وأنزل اللّٰه تصديق قول النبي ﷺ: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللّٰهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللّٰهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٦٨].
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠٠٩)، ومسلم (٨٦)، والسياق لمسلم.

14084 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“Which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah?”
He replied:
“That you set up an equal with Allah even though He created you.”
I said:
“That is indeed tremendous.”
Then I asked:
“Then which?”
He replied:
“That you kill your child out of fear that he will eat with you.”
I asked:
“Then which?”
He replied:
“That you commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife.”
Another narration adds that Allah revealed in confirmation of the Prophet’s ﷺ words:
“And those who do not invoke another deity alongside Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except with right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty.”
 [Sūrat al-Furqān 25:68]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6009) and Muslim (86). The context is that of Muslim.

١٤٠٨٥ — عن أبي قتادة الأنصاري أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يصلي وهو حامل أمامة بنت زينب بنت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ولأبي العاص بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس، فإذا سجد وضعها، وإذا قام حملها.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في جامع الصلاة (٨٧)، والبخاري (٥١٦)، ومسلم (٥٤٣: ٤١).
