14455 — Laqīṭ ibn Ṣabirah narrated:
I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he slaughtered a sheep for us.
He said:
“Do not think that we slaughtered it specifically because of you. Rather, we own sheep, and whenever their number reaches one hundred, we slaughter one.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (16382).
There is also a longer story in this hadith, narrated by Aḥmad (16384) from ʿAbd al-Razzāq—and it is in his Muṣannaf (80)—and by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (19/215), with an authentic chain, from ʿĀṣim ibn Laqīṭ ibn Ṣabirah, from his father, the delegate of Banū al-Muntafiq.
He said:
A companion and I set out until we reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but we did not find him.
ʿĀʾishah gave us dates to eat and prepared a thick porridge for us.
Then the Prophet ﷺ arrived, walking briskly, and asked:
“Have you been given anything to eat?”
We replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
While we were there, the shepherd drove the sheep into their enclosure carrying a newborn lamb.
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“Has one been born?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
“Then slaughter a sheep for us.”
Then he turned toward us and said:
“Do not think that we slaughtered the sheep specifically because of the two of you. We have one hundred sheep, and we do not wish their number to increase beyond that. Whenever the shepherd receives a newborn lamb, we instruct him to slaughter a sheep.”
Laqīṭ then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, tell me about wuḍūʾ.”
He replied:
“When you perform wuḍūʾ, perform it thoroughly and pass water between the fingers. When drawing water into your nose, do so thoroughly unless you are fasting.”
He said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I have a wife…”
and he mentioned the harshness of her speech and the harm she caused him.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Divorce her.”
He replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, she has been my companion for a long time and we have children.”
He said:
“Then keep her and instruct her. If there is good in her, she will respond. And do not strike your wife as you would strike your slave woman.”

١٤٤٥٦ — عن أبي جحيفة وهب السوائي قال: آخى النبي ﷺ بين سلمان وأبي الدرداء، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء، فرأى أم الدرداء متبذلة، فقال لها: ما شأنك؟ قالت: أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا. فجاء أبو الدرداء، فصنع له طعامًا، فقال: كل، فإني صائم. قال: ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل. فأكل. فلما كان الليل ذهب أبو الدرداء يقوم، فقال: نم. فنام. ثم ذهب يقوم، فقال: نم. فلما كان آخر الليل قال سلمان: قم الآن. قال: فصليا. فقال له سلمان: إن لربك عليك حقًا، ولنفسك عليك حقًا، ولأهلك عليك حقًا، فأعط كل ذي حق حقه. فأتى النبي ﷺ فذكر ذلك له، فقال النبي ﷺ:
((صدق سلمان)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦١٣٩).

14456 — Abū Juḥayfah Wahb al-Suwāʾī narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ established a bond of brotherhood between Salmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ.
Salmān visited Abū al-Dardāʾ and saw Umm al-Dardāʾ dressed in a neglected manner.
He asked her:
“What is the matter with you?”

١٤٤٥٦ — عن أبي جحيفة وهب السوائي قال: آخى النبي ﷺ بين سلمان وأبي الدرداء، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء، فرأى أم الدرداء متبذلة، فقال لها: ما شأنك؟ قالت: أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا. فجاء أبو الدرداء، فصنع له طعامًا، فقال: كل، فإني صائم. قال: ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل. فأكل. فلما كان الليل ذهب أبو الدرداء يقوم، فقال: نم. فنام. ثم ذهب يقوم، فقال: نم. فلما كان آخر الليل قال سلمان: قم الآن. قال: فصليا. فقال له سلمان: إن لربك عليك حقًا، ولنفسك عليك حقًا، ولأهلك عليك حقًا، فأعط كل ذي حق حقه. فأتى النبي ﷺ فذكر ذلك له، فقال النبي ﷺ:
((صدق سلمان)).

١٤٤٥٧ — عن أبي موسى قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يركب الحمار، ويلبس الصوف، ويعتقل الشاة، ويأتي مراعاة الضيف.
صحيح: رواه أبو الشيخ في أخلاق النبي ﷺ (٣١٥)، والحاكم (١/٦١)، والبيهقي في الكبرى (٢/٤٢٠).
قلت: لا تعارض بين حديث أبي موسى وبين حديث المغيرة بن شعبة، فإن لباس الصوف في الغالب يستعمل في الشتاء، فقصة المغيرة وإن كانت وقعت مرة واحدة، ولكن لا يمنع استمرار استعماله في الشتاء، وهذا الذي يظهر من حديث أبي موسى.

english_source:
14457 — Abū Mūsā narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ride a donkey, wear wool, personally restrain a sheep, and attend to the needs of his guest.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū al-Shaykh in Akhlāq al-Nabī ﷺ (315), al-Ḥākim (1/61), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (2/420).
The author states:
There is no contradiction between the hadith of Abū Mūsā and the hadith of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.
Woolen clothing is generally worn in winter. Although the incident involving al-Mughīrah may have occurred only once, that does not prevent the Prophet ﷺ from having continued to wear wool during the winter.
This is what appears from the hadith of Abū Mūsā.

١٤٤٥٩ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أنها قالت: كان في بريرة ثلاث سنن: خيرت على زوجها حين عتقت، وأهدي لها لحم، فدخل علي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ والبرمة على النار، فدعا بطعام، فأتي بخبز وأدم من أدم البيت، فقال:
((ألم أر برمة على النار فيها لحم؟)).
فقالوا: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه، ذلك لحم تصدق به على بريرة، فكرهنا أن نطعمك منه. فقال:
((هو عليها صدقة، وهو منها لنا هدية)).
وقال النبي ﷺ فيها:
((إنما الولاء لمن أعتق)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٤٣٠)، ومسلم (١٥٠٤: ١٤)، واللفظ لمسلم.

14459 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
There were three legal rulings connected to Barīrah.
She was given the choice regarding her husband when she was emancipated.
Some meat was given to her in charity.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me while a cooking pot was over the fire.
He asked for food, and bread with a household condiment was brought to him.
He said:
“Did I not see a pot over the fire containing meat?”
They replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah, but that is meat which was given in charity to Barīrah, and we disliked giving you some of it.”
He said:
“It was charity for her, but from her it is a gift to us.”
The Prophet ﷺ also said concerning her:
“The right of walāʾ belongs only to the one who emancipates the slave.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5430) and Muslim (1504:14). The wording is that of Muslim.

14460 — Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī narrated:
There was a man from the Anṣār known as Abū Shuʿayb who had a servant who worked as a butcher.
He saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and recognized signs of hunger on his face.
He said to his servant:
“Prepare food for five people, for I want to invite the Prophet ﷺ as one of five.”
The servant prepared the food.
Abū Shuʿayb then went to the Prophet ﷺ and invited him as one of five people.
Another man followed them without having been invited.
When they reached the door, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“This man followed us. If you wish, you may give him permission, and if you wish, he may return.”
The host replied:
“No, rather I give him permission, O Messenger of Allah.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5434) and Muslim (2036:138). The wording is that of Muslim.

١٤٤٦١ — عن أنس بن مالك أن جارًا لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ فارسيًا كان طيب المرق، فصنع لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ ثم جاء يدعوه، فقال:
((وهذه؟)).
لعائشة. فقال: لا. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لا)).
فعاد يدعوه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((وهذه؟)).
قال: لا. قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لا)).
ثم عاد يدعوه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((وهذه؟)).
قال: نعم، في الثالثة. فقاما يتدافعان حتى أتيا منزله.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٣٧).
لأن النبي ﷺ وجد أن عائشة رضي اللّٰه عنها أيضًا كان بها من الجوع، فكره النبي ﷺ أن يستأثر عليها بالأكل دونها. وهذا من مكارم أخلاق النبي ﷺ، وخصوصًا مع أهل بيته.
وقد استحب مالك أن الرجل إذا أكرم رجلًا فدعاه إلى طعام فمن الأفضل أن يبعث إليه بذلك الطعام ليأكل مع أهله.

14461 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
A Persian neighbor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was skilled at preparing broth.
He prepared some food for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and came to invite him.
The Prophet ﷺ asked, referring to ʿĀʾishah:
“And her?”
The man replied:
“No.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Then no.”
The man returned and invited him again.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“And her?”
He replied:
“No.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ again said:
“Then no.”
The man returned a third time and invited him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“And her?”
This time the man replied:
“Yes.”
So the Prophet ﷺ and ʿĀʾishah got up and hurried together until they reached his house.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2037).
The author explains that the Prophet ﷺ recognized that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was also hungry, so he disliked eating without her and taking the food for himself.
This was from the noble character of the Prophet ﷺ, especially in his conduct toward his household.
Mālik also considered it recommended that if a person wishes to honor someone by inviting him to food, it is even better to send some of that food to him so that he may eat it together with his family.

١٤٤٦٢ — عن أنس قال: كنت غلامًا أمشي مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فدخل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على غلام له خياط، فأتاه بقصعة فيها طعام وعليه دباء، فجعل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يتتبع الدباء. قال: فلما رأيت ذلك جعلت أجمعه بين يديه. قال: فأقبل الغلام على عمله. قال أنس: لا أزال أحب الدباء بعد ما رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ صنع ما صنع.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٤٣٥)، ومسلم (٢٠٤١).

14462 — Anas narrated:
I was a young boy walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon a servant of his who was a tailor.
The tailor brought him a bowl containing food with gourd in it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began seeking out the pieces of gourd.
When I saw that, I began gathering the pieces of gourd and placing them in front of him.
Meanwhile, the tailor returned to his work.
Anas said:
“I have continued to love gourd ever since I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do what he did.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5435) and Muslim (2041).

١٤٤٦٣ — عن أنس أن أم سليم أمه عمدت إلى مد من شعير فجشته، وجعلت منه خطيفة، وعصرت عكة عندها، ثم بعثتني إلى النبي ﷺ فأتيته وهو في أصحابه فدعوته، قال:
((ومن معي؟)).

((أدخل علي عشرة)).

14463 — Anas narrated:
My mother, Umm Sulaym, took a mudd of barley, ground it, and prepared a thick dish from it. She also squeezed some fat from a leather container she had.
Then she sent me to the Prophet ﷺ.
I found him among his Companions and invited him.
He asked:
“And those who are with me?”
I returned and said:
“He is asking, ‘And those who are with me?’”
Abū Ṭalḥah went out to him and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, it is only a little food prepared by Umm Sulaym.”
The Prophet ﷺ entered, and the food was brought.
He said:
“Admit ten people to me.”
Ten entered and ate until they were full.
Then he said:
“Admit ten more.”
Another ten entered and ate until they were full.
Then he again said:
“Admit ten.”
This continued until forty had been counted.
Then the Prophet ﷺ ate and stood up.
Anas said:
“I kept looking at the food to see whether any of it had diminished.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5450) and Muslim (2040).

١٤٤٦٤ — عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر أن أبا بكر تضيف رهطًا، فقال لعبد الرحمن: دونك أضيافك، فإني منطلق إلى النبي ﷺ، فافرغ من قراهم قبل أن أجيء. فانطلق عبد الرحمن فأتاهم بما عنده، فقال: اطعموا. فقالوا: أين رب منزلنا؟ قال: اطعموا. قالوا: ما نحن بآكلين حتى يجيء رب منزلنا. قال: اقبلوا عنا قراكم، فإنه إن جاء ولم تطعموا لنلقين منه. فأبوا، فعرفت أنه يجد علي. فلما جاء تنحيت عنه، فقال: ما صنعتم؟ فأخبروه، فقال: يا عبد الرحمن. فسكت. ثم قال: يا عبد الرحمن. فسكت. فقال: يا غنثر، أقسمت عليك إن كنت تسمع صوتي لما جئت. فخرجت، فقلت: سل ضيافك. فقالوا: صدق، أتانا به. قال: فإنما انتظرتموني؟ واللّٰه لا أطعمه الليلة. فقال الآخرون: واللّٰه لا نطعمه حتى تطعمه. قال: لم أر في الشر كالليلة! ويلكم، ما أنتم؟ لم لا تقبلون عنا قراكم؟ هات طعامك. فجاءه، فوضع يده فقال: باسم اللّٰه، الأولى للشيطان. فأكل وأكلوا.
وزاد مسلم: فلما أصبح غدا على النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، بروا وحنثت. قال: فأخبره، فقال:
((بل أنت أبرهم وأخيرهم)).
قال: ولم تبلغني كفارة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٤٠)، ومسلم (٢٠٥٧: ١٧٧).

14464 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated:
Abū Bakr hosted a group of guests and said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān:
“Take care of your guests, for I am going to the Prophet ﷺ. Finish serving them before I return.”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān brought them whatever food was available and said:
“Eat.”
They asked:
“Where is the master of the house?”
He replied:
“Eat.”
They said:
“We will not eat until the master of the house comes.”
He said:
“Please accept your hospitality from us. If he returns and you have not eaten, I will surely face trouble from him.”
But they refused.
I realized that Abū Bakr would be angry with me.
When he returned, I moved away from him.
He asked:
“What did you do?”
The guests told him what had happened.
He called:
“O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān!”
I remained silent.
He called again:
“O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān!”
I remained silent.
Then he said:
“O foolish fellow! I adjure you, if you can hear my voice, come here!”
So I came out and said:
“Ask your guests.”
They said:
“He is telling the truth. He brought us the food.”
Abū Bakr said:
“So you were only waiting for me? By Allah, I will not eat it tonight.”
The guests replied:
“By Allah, we will not eat until you eat.”
Abū Bakr said:
“I have never seen a night as troublesome as this! Woe to you, what is wrong with you? Why will you not accept our hospitality? Bring the food.”
The food was brought.
He placed his hand into it and said:
“In the Name of Allah. My first oath was from Satan.”
Then he ate, and they ate with him.
Muslim adds:
The next morning Abū Bakr went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, they fulfilled their oath while I broke mine.”
He told him what had happened.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Rather, you were the most righteous and the best of them.”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:
“No expiation for an oath reached me in connection with this incident.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6140) and Muslim (2057:177).

“O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān!”
I remained silent.
He called again:
“O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān!”
I remained silent.
Then he said:
“O foolish fellow! I adjure you, if you can hear my voice, come here!”
So I came out and said:
“Ask your guests.”
They said:
“He is telling the truth. He brought us the food.”
Abū Bakr said:
“So you were only waiting for me? By Allah, I will not eat it tonight.”
The guests replied:
“By Allah, we will not eat until you eat.”
Abū Bakr said:
“I have never seen a night as troublesome as this! Woe to you, what is wrong with you? Why will you not accept our hospitality? Bring the food.”
The food was brought.
He placed his hand into it and said:
“In the Name of Allah. My first oath was from Satan.”
Then he ate, and they ate with him.
Muslim adds:
The next morning Abū Bakr went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, they fulfilled their oath while I broke mine.”
He told him what had happened.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Rather, you were the most righteous and the best of them.”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:
“No expiation for an oath reached me in connection with this incident.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6140) and Muslim (2057:177).

14465 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated:
Abū Bakr brought home a guest—or some guests—then remained with the Prophet ﷺ until evening.
When he returned, my mother said to him:
“You remained away from your guest—or your guests—tonight.”
He asked:
“Did you not give them dinner?”
She replied:
“We offered it to him—or to them—but he refused—or they refused.”
Abū Bakr became angry, rebuked and scolded, and swore that he would not eat the food.
I hid myself.
He called out:
“O foolish fellow!”
His wife then swore that she would not eat until he ate, and the guest—or guests—swore that he would not eat—or they would not eat—until Abū Bakr ate.
Abū Bakr said:
“This seems to be from Satan.”
He called for the food, then ate, and they ate with him.
Whenever they lifted a morsel, more food than it had been would grow underneath it.
Abū Bakr said:
“O sister of Banū Firās, what is this?”
She replied:
“By the delight of my eye, it is now more than it was before we began eating.”
They ate from it, and some of it was sent to the Prophet ﷺ. It was mentioned that he also ate from it.

١٤٤٦٧ — عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((لا تصاحب إلا مؤمنًا، ولا يأكل طعامك إلا تقي)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٨٣٢)، والترمذي (٢٣٩٥)، وأحمد (١١٣٣٧)، والدارمي (٥٥٤)، والحاكم (٤/١٢٨).
قوله: “لا يأكل طعامك إلا تقي” هذا في طعام الدعوة العامة، ويستثنى منهم أصحاب الحقوق من الجيران والأقارب وأصحاب الحاجة والذين يخاف من شرهم.

14467 — Abū Saʿīd narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not keep close companionship except with a believer, and let none but a God-fearing person eat your food.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4832), al-Tirmidhī (2395), Aḥmad (11337), al-Dārimī (554), and al-Ḥākim (4/128).
The words:
“Let none but a God-fearing person eat your food”
refer to food offered through a general invitation.
Those who possess established rights are excepted from this, such as neighbors, relatives, people in need, and those whose harm is feared.

١٤٤٦٨ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ضافه ضيف كافر، فأمر له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بشاة حلبت، فشرب حلابها، ثم أخرى فشربه، ثم أخرى فشربه، حتى شرب حلاب سبع شياه، ثم إنه أصبح فأسلم، فأمر له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بشاة فحلبت، فشرب حلابها، ثم أمر له بأخرى، فلم يستتمها، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((المؤمن يشرب في معى واحد، والكافر يشرب في سبعة أمعاء)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في صفة النبي ﷺ (١٠)، ومسلم (٢٠٦٣: ١٨٦)، والبخاري (٥٣٩٦).

english_source:
14468 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ hosted a disbelieving guest.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a sheep be milked for him, and he drank all of its milk.
Then another was milked and he drank its milk, then another, until he had drunk the milk of seven sheep.
The next morning he embraced Islam.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a sheep be milked for him, and he drank its milk.
Then another was milked for him, but he could not finish it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The believer drinks with one intestine, while the disbeliever drinks with seven intestines.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ṣifat al-Nabī ﷺ (10), Muslim (2063:186), and al-Bukhārī (5396).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك في صفة النبي ﷺ (١٠)، ومسلم (٢٠٦٣: ١٨٦)، والبخاري (٥٣٩٦).
14468 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ hosted a disbelieving guest.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a sheep be milked for him, and he drank all of its milk.
Then another was milked and he drank its milk, then another, until he had drunk the milk of seven sheep.
The next morning he embraced Islam.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a sheep be milked for him, and he drank its milk.
Then another was milked for him, but he could not finish it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The believer drinks with one intestine, while the disbeliever drinks with seven intestines.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ṣifat al-Nabī ﷺ (10), Muslim (2063:186), and al-Bukhārī (5396).

١٤٤٦٩ — عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر أن أصحاب الصفة كانوا أناسًا فقراء، وأن النبي ﷺ قال:
((من كان عنده طعام اثنين فليذهب بثالث، وإن أربع فخامس أو سادس)).
وأن أبا بكر جاء بثلاثة، فانطلق النبي ﷺ بعشرة. قال: فهو أنا وأبي وأمي - فلا أدري قال: وامرأتي وخادم - بيننا وبين بيت أبي بكر. وإن أبا بكر تعشى عند النبي ﷺ، ثم لبث حيث صليت العشاء، ثم رجع فلبث حتى نعس النبي ﷺ، فجاء بعد ما مضى من الليل ما شاء اللّٰه. قالت له امرأته: وما حبسك عن أضيافك - أو قالت: ضيفك؟ - قال: أوما عشيتيهم؟ قالت: أبوا حتى تجيء، قد عرضوا فأبوا. قال: فذهبت أنا فاختبأت، فقال: يا غنثر. فجدع وسب، وقال: كلوا لا هنيئًا. فقال: والله لا أطعمه أبدًا. وأيم اللّٰه، ما كنا نأخذ من لقمة إلا ربا من أسفلها أكثر منها - قال: يعني حتى شبعوا - وصارت أكثر مما كانت قبل ذلك. فنظر إليها أبو بكر فإذا هي كما هي أو أكثر منها، فقال لامرأته: يا أخت بني فراس، ما هذا؟ قالت: لا وقرة عيني، لهي الآن أكثر منها قبل ذلك بثلاث مرات. فأكل منها أبو بكر، وقال: إنما كان ذلك من الشيطان - يعني يمينه - ثم أكل منها لقمة، ثم حملها إلى النبي ﷺ فأصبحت عنده. وكان بيننا وبين قوم عقد، فمضى الأجل، ففرقنا اثني عشر رجلًا، مع كل رجل منهم أناس، اللّٰه أعلم كم مع كل رجل، فأكلوا منها أجمعون، أو كما قال.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠٢)، ومسلم (٢٠٥٧: ١٧٦).

14469 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated:
The people of al-Ṣuffah were poor people.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever has food sufficient for two should take a third person with him, and whoever has food for four should take a fifth or a sixth.”
Abū Bakr brought three people home, while the Prophet ﷺ took ten.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:
The household consisted of me, my father, and my mother—and I do not know whether he also mentioned my wife and a servant shared between our household and the household of Abū Bakr.
Abū Bakr ate dinner with the Prophet ﷺ, then remained until after the ʿIshāʾ prayer.
He stayed until the Prophet ﷺ became drowsy, then returned after as much of the night had passed as Allah willed.
His wife asked him:
“What kept you from your guests—or your guest?”
He replied:
“Did you not serve them dinner?”
She said:
“They refused to eat until you came. Food was offered to them, but they refused.”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:
I went and hid myself.
Abū Bakr called:
“O foolish fellow!”
He rebuked and insulted me, then said to the guests:
“Eat, though may it bring you no enjoyment!”
Then he said:
“By Allah, I will never eat it.”
By Allah, whenever we took a morsel from the food, more than that amount grew beneath it, until everyone became full.
The food became greater in quantity than it had been before.
Abū Bakr looked at it and saw that it was still as much as before, or even more.
He said to his wife:
“O sister of Banū Firās, what is this?”
She replied:
“By the delight of my eye, it is now three times as much as it was before.”
Abū Bakr then ate from it and said:
“That oath of mine was only from Satan.”
Then he ate a morsel and carried the food to the Prophet ﷺ, where it remained until morning.
There was a treaty between us and another people, and when its term expired, we divided ourselves into twelve groups, each man accompanied by a number of people—Allah knows how many were with each one—and they all ate from that food.
Or words to that effect.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (602) and Muslim (2057:176).

١٤٤٧٠ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: لم أعقل أبوي إلا وهما يدينان الدين، ولم يمر عليهما يوم إلا يأتينا فيه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ طرفي النهار، بكرة وعشية. فبينما نحن جلوس في بيت أبي بكر في نحر الظهيرة، قال قائل: هذا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في ساعة لم يكن يأتينا فيها. قال أبو بكر: ما جاء به في هذه الساعة إلا أمر. قال:
((إني قد أذن لي بالخروج)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٠٧٩).

14470 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
I never knew my parents except that they both followed the religion of Islam.
Not a day passed without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening.
One day, while we were sitting in the house of Abū Bakr at the height of midday, someone said:
“Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming at an hour when he does not normally come.”
Abū Bakr said:
“Nothing but an important matter could have brought him at this hour.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I have been given permission to depart.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6079).

١٤٤٧٠ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: لم أعقل أبوي إلا وهما يدينان الدين، ولم يمر عليهما يوم إلا يأتينا فيه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ طرفي النهار، بكرة وعشية. فبينما نحن جلوس في بيت أبي بكر في نحر الظهيرة، قال قائل: هذا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في ساعة لم يكن يأتينا فيها. قال أبو بكر: ما جاء به في هذه الساعة إلا أمر. قال:
((إني قد أذن لي بالخروج)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٠٧٩).
14470 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
I never knew my parents except that they both followed the religion of Islam.
Not a day passed without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening.
One day, while we were sitting in the house of Abū Bakr at the height of midday, someone said:
“Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming at an hour when he does not normally come.”
Abū Bakr said:
“Nothing but an important matter could have brought him at this hour.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I have been given permission to depart.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6079).

١٤٤٧٢ — عن أنس بن مالك أن أم سليم كانت تبسط للنبي ﷺ نطعًا، فيقيل عندها على ذلك النطع. قال: فإذا نام النبي ﷺ أخذت من عرقه وشعره، فجمعته في قارورة، ثم جمعته في سك. قال: فلما حضر أنس بن مالك الوفاة أوصى إلي أن يجعل في حنوطه من ذلك السك، قال: فجعل في حنوطه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٨١)، ومسلم (٢٣٣١).
قوله: “فلما حضر أنس الوفاة” القائل هو ثمامة.

english_source:
14472 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
Umm Sulaym used to spread a leather mat for the Prophet ﷺ, and he would take his midday nap upon it in her home.
When the Prophet ﷺ slept, she would collect some of his perspiration and hair and place them in a bottle, then mix them into perfume.
When the time of Anas ibn Mālik’s death approached, he instructed that some of that perfume be placed in the aromatic mixture used for his burial.
So it was placed in his burial perfume.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6281) and Muslim (2331).
Regarding the words:
“When the death of Anas approached,”
the speaker here is Thumāmah.

“When one of you puts on his footwear, let him begin with the right foot. When he removes it, let him begin with the left. Let the right foot be the first to be shod and the last to be uncovered.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in al-Libās (15), al-Bukhārī (5855), and Muslim (2097).

١٤٤٧٥ — عن أم المؤمنين عائشة قالت: كان النبي ﷺ يعجبه التيمن في تنعله، وترجله، وطهوره، وفي شأنه كله.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٨)، ومسلم (٢٦٨).
استحباب التيمن يحمل على ما كان من العبادة والزينة، بخلاف ما كان للضرورة فلا بأس بالشمال.

14475 — The Mother of the Believers ʿĀʾishah narrated:
“The Prophet ﷺ liked to begin with the right side when putting on his footwear, combing his hair, purifying himself, and in all his affairs.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (168) and Muslim (268).
The recommendation of beginning with the right applies to matters of worship and adornment.
As for matters dictated by necessity, there is no harm in using the left side.

arabic_source:
١٤٤٧٨ — عن جابر قال: نهى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن ينتعل الرجل قائمًا.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤١٣٥).
فقه الحديث: النهي يحمل على التوجيه والإرشاد، فإن لبس النعال قائمًا قد لا يمكن اللابس من لبسه جيدًا، ولكن إن كان لبس النعال قاعدًا فيه إحراج للآخرين، فلا بأس أن ينتعل قائمًا؛ لأن الشريعة جاءت لرفع الحرج، ولذا لا أعرف من حمل النهي على التحريم.

english_source:
14478 — Jābir narrated:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prohibited a man from putting on his footwear while standing.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4135).
Juristic Understanding of the Hadith
The prohibition is understood as guidance and instruction rather than an absolute prohibition.
Putting on footwear while standing may prevent a person from putting it on properly.
However, if sitting down to put on footwear would inconvenience other people, there is no harm in putting it on while standing, because the Sacred Law came to remove hardship.
For this reason, the author states that he does not know of anyone who interpreted this prohibition as making the act unlawful.

١٤٤٧٩ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((لا يمشين أحدكم في نعل واحدة، لينعلهما جميعًا، أو ليحفهما جميعًا)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في اللباس (١٤)، والبخاري (٥٨٥٦)، ومسلم (٢٠٩٧: ٦٨).

١٤٤٨٠ — عن أبي رزين قال: خرج إلينا أبو هريرة، فضرب بيده على جبهته، فقال: ألا إنكم تحدثون أني أكذب على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لتهتدوا وأضل؟ ألا وإني أشهد لسمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((إذا انقطع شسع أحدكم فلا يمش في الأخرى حتى يصلحها)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٩٨).

14480 — Abū Razīn narrated:
Abū Hurayrah came out to us and struck his forehead with his hand, saying:
“Do you claim that I lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that you may be guided while I go astray? I testify that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘If the strap of one of your sandals breaks, he should not walk in the other sandal until he repairs it.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2098).

١٤٤٨٢ — عن جابر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ - أو قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول -:
((إذا انقطع شسع أحدكم - أو من انقطع شسع نعله - فلا يمش في نعل واحدة حتى يصلح شسعه، ولا يمش في خف واحد، ولا يأكل بشماله، ولا يحتبي بالثوب الواحد، ولا يلتحف الصماء)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٩٩: ٧١).
قوله: “شسع” هو سيور النعل، وهو الذي يدخل بين الإصبعين، ويدخل في الثقب الذي في صدر النعل المشدود في الزمام، وجمعه شسوع.

14482 — Jābir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said—or he said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say”:
“If the strap of one of your sandals breaks, do not walk in only one sandal until you repair its strap. Do not walk in only one leather sock, do not eat with your left hand, do not sit in the iḥtibāʾ posture while wrapped in a single garment, and do not wrap yourself in the ṣammāʾ manner.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2099:71).
The word “shisʿ” refers to the sandal strap that passes between the toes and through the hole at the front of the sandal where it is secured to the upper strap.
Its plural is shusūʿ.

١٤٤٨٦ — عن يحيى بن أبي إسحاق قال: قال لي سالم بن عبد اللّٰه: ما الإستبرق؟ قلت: ما غلظ من الديباج وخشن منه. قال: سمعت عبد اللّٰه يقول: رأى عمر على رجل حلة من إستبرق، فأتى بها النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، اشتر هذه فالبسها لوفد الناس إذا قدموا عليك. فقال:
((إنما يلبس الحرير من لا خلاق له)).
فمضى من ذلك ما مضى، ثم إن النبي ﷺ بعث إليه بحلة، فأتى بها النبي ﷺ فقال: بعثت إلي بهذه، وقد قلت في مثلها ما قلت؟ قال:
((إنما بعثت إليك لتصيب بها مالًا)).
فكان ابن عمر يكره العلم في الثوب لهذا الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠٨١)، ومسلم (٢٠٦٨: ٩٠).
فائدة
قال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًا يُوَارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ وَرِيشًا وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللّٰهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ [سورة الأعراف: ٢٦].
اللباس على قسمين:
١- قسم يستر به العورات، وأشار إليه بقوله: ﴿لِبَاسًا يُوَارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ﴾.
٢- وقسم يلبس للزينة والجمال، وأشار إليه بقوله: ﴿وَرِيشًا﴾. يقال: ريش ورياش، والريش هو للطائر، وهو بمثابة اللباس له. امتن اللّٰه علينا بأنه أنزل من اللباس ما هو الضروري، كما أنزل من اللباس ما هو المقصود منه الزينة والجمال؛ لأنه كما جاء في الصحيح:
((إن اللّٰه جميل يحب الجمال)).
رواه مسلم (١٤٧).

english_source:
14486 — Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated:
Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh asked me:
“What is istabraq?”
I replied:
“It is thick, coarse brocade.”
He said:
I heard ʿAbdullāh say:
ʿUmar saw a man wearing a garment of istabraq. He brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, buy this and wear it when delegations come to you.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Silk is only worn by one who has no share in the Hereafter.”
Some time passed, then the Prophet ﷺ sent ʿUmar a garment.
ʿUmar brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“You sent this to me even though you said what you said concerning a garment like it?”
He replied:
“I only sent it to you so that you might obtain some wealth through it.”
Because of this hadith, Ibn ʿUmar disliked decorative silk stripes in clothing.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6081) and Muslim (2068:90).
Benefit
Allah, the Exalted, says:
“O children of Adam, We have indeed sent down to you clothing that covers your private parts and clothing for adornment. But the clothing of taqwā—that is best. That is from the signs of Allah so that they may remember.”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:26]
Clothing is of two types:
Clothing used to cover the private parts, which is indicated by Allah’s words:
“clothing that covers your private parts.”
Clothing worn for adornment and beauty, which is indicated by His words:
“and clothing for adornment.”
The Arabic words rīsh and riyāsh are used in this meaning. Rīsh originally refers to the feathers of a bird, which serve as its clothing and adornment.
Allah has bestowed upon us clothing that fulfills the essential need of covering the body, just as He has bestowed clothing intended for beauty and adornment.
This is consistent with what is authentically narrated:
“Indeed, Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty.”
Narrated by Muslim (147).

“O children of Adam, We have indeed sent down to you clothing that covers your private parts and clothing for adornment. But the clothing of taqwā—that is best. That is from the signs of Allah so that they may remember.”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:26]
Clothing is of two types:
Clothing used to cover the private parts, which is indicated by Allah’s words:
“clothing that covers your private parts.”
Clothing worn for adornment and beauty, which is indicated by His words:
“and clothing for adornment.”
The Arabic words rīsh and riyāsh are used in this meaning. Rīsh originally refers to the feathers of a bird, which serve as its clothing and adornment.
Allah has bestowed upon us clothing that fulfills the essential need of covering the body, just as He has bestowed clothing intended for beauty and adornment.
This is consistent with what is authentically narrated:
“Indeed, Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty.”
Narrated by Muslim (147).

١٤٤٨٨ — عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن أحب أسمائكم إلى اللّٰه عبد اللّٰه وعبد الرحمن)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٣٢).
وأما ما جاء في الصحيحين: البخاري (٢٨٦٤)، ومسلم (١٧٧٦)، كلاهما من حديث البراء بن عازب، عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال:
((أنا النبي لا كذب… أنا ابن عبد المطلب)).
فأجاب عنه ابن القيم بقوله: أما قوله: ((أنا ابن عبد المطلب))، فهذا ليس من باب إنشاء التسمية بذلك، وإنما هو من باب الإخبار بالاسم الذي عرف به المسمى دون غيره، والإخبار بمثل ذلك على وجه تعريف المسمى لا يحرم، ولا وجه لتخصيص أبي محمد بن حزم ذلك بعبد المطلب خاصة، فقد كان الصحابة يسمون بني عبد شمس، وبني عبد الدار بأسمائهم، ولا ينكر عليهم النبي ﷺ، فباب الإخبار أوسع من باب الإنشاء، فيجوز ما لا يجوز في الإنشاء”. تحفة المودود (ص ١٨٩).

14488 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The most beloved of your names to Allah are ʿAbdullāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2132).
As for what is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections—al-Bukhārī (2864) and Muslim (1776)—from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I am the Prophet, there is no lie… I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.”
Ibn al-Qayyim answered this by saying:
“His statement, ‘I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib,’ does not constitute newly assigning such a name. Rather, it is simply identifying a person by the name through which he is known. Informing others of such a name for the purpose of identification is not prohibited. There is no basis for Abū Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm restricting this specifically to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. The Companions used to refer to Banū ʿAbd Shams and Banū ʿAbd al-Dār by those names, and the Prophet ﷺ did not object. The category of reporting and identification is broader than the category of newly assigning a name, so something may be permissible in reporting that would not be permissible when newly naming someone.”
Tuḥfat al-Mawdūd, p. 189.

١٤٤٨٩ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال: لما قدمت نجران سألوني، فقالوا: إنكم تقرؤون: ﴿يَا أُخْتَ هَارُونَ﴾، وموسى قبل عيسى بكذا وكذا. فلما قدمت على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ سألته عن ذلك، فقال:
((إنهم كانوا يسمون بأنبيائهم والصالحين قبلهم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٣٥).

14489 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah narrated:
When I came to Najrān, they questioned me and said:
“You recite, ‘O sister of Hārūn,’ yet Mūsā lived such-and-such a long time before ʿĪsā.”
When I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I asked him about this.
He said:
“They used to name people after the Prophets and righteous people who came before them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2135).

١٤٤٩٠ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: ولد لي غلام، فأتيت به النبي ﷺ فسماه إبراهيم، وحنكه بتمرة، ودعا له بالبركة، ودفعه إلي، وكان أكبر ولد أبي موسى.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٩٨)، ومسلم (٢١٤٥)، واللفظ للبخاري.

14490 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated:
A son was born to me, so I brought him to the Prophet ﷺ.
He named him Ibrāhīm, performed taḥnīk for him with a date, supplicated for blessing for him, and handed him back to me.
He was the eldest son of Abū Mūsā.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6198) and Muslim (2145). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٤٤٩١ — عن يوسف بن عبد اللّٰه بن سلام يقول: أجلسني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في حجره، ومسح على رأسي، وسماني يوسف.

١٤٤٩٢ — عن أبي بكر بن محمد بن عمرو بن حزم، عن أبيه قال: إن عمر بن الخطاب جمع كل غلام اسمه اسم نبي، فأدخلهم دارًا، وأراد أن يغير أسماءهم، فشهد آباؤهم أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ سماهم. قال: وكان أبي محمد بن عمرو بن حزم فيهم.
حسن: رواه إسحاق بن راهويه كما في المطالب (٢٧٩٦).

١٤٤٩٣ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب أن النبي ﷺ كان لا يتطير من شيء، وكان إذا بعث عاملًا سأل عن اسمه، فإذا أعجبه اسمه فرح به، ورئي بشر ذلك في وجهه، وإن كره اسمه رئي كراهية ذلك في وجهه، وإذا دخل قرية سأل عن اسمها، فإن أعجبه اسمها فرح، ورئي بشر ذلك في وجهه، وإن كره اسمها رئي كراهية ذلك في وجهه.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٩٢٠)، والنسائي في الكبرى (٨٧٧١)، وأحمد (٢٢٩٤٦)، وابن حبان (٥٨٢٧).

english_source:
14493 — Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ did not regard anything as an evil omen.
When he appointed a man to a task, he would ask his name.
If he liked the man’s name, he would be pleased by it and signs of happiness would be visible on his face.
If he disliked the name, signs of dislike would be visible on his face.
Likewise, when he entered a town or village, he would ask its name.
If he liked its name, he would be pleased and signs of happiness would be visible on his face.
If he disliked its name, signs of dislike would be visible on his face.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3920), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8771), Aḥmad (22946), and Ibn Ḥibbān (5827).

14494 — Yaʿīsh al-Ghifārī narrated:
One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a she-camel and asked:
“Who will milk her?”
A man said:
“I will.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What is your name?”
He replied:
“Murrah.”
He said:
“Sit down.”
Another man stood.
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What is your name?”
He replied:
“Jamrah.”
He said:
“Sit down.”
Then Yaʿīsh stood.
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What is your name?”
He replied:
“Yaʿīsh.”
He said:
“Milk her.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (22/277).

١٤٤٩٥ — عن المسور بن مخرمة ومروان، يصدق كل واحد منهما حديث صاحبه، قالا: خرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ زمن الحديبية… الحديث بطوله، وفيه: قال معمر: فأخبرني أيوب، عن عكرمة: أنه لما جاء سهيل بن عمرو قال النبي ﷺ:
((لقد سهل لكم من أمركم)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٣١).

14495 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwān narrated, each confirming the other’s account:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyyah…
to the end of the lengthy hadith.
It includes the statement of Maʿmar:
Ayyūb informed me, from ʿIkrimah, that when Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Your matter has now been made easy for you.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2731).

١٤٤٩٦ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أن النبي ﷺ مر بأرض تسمى غدرة، فسماها خضرة.

١٤٤٩٨ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه الأنصاري قال: ولد لرجل منا غلام فسماه القاسم، فقالت الأنصار: لا نكنيك أبا القاسم، ولا ننعمك عينًا. فأتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ولد لي غلام فسميته القاسم، فقالت الأنصار: لا نكنيك أبا القاسم، ولا ننعمك عينًا. فقال النبي ﷺ:
((أحسنت الأنصار، سموا باسمي، ولا تكنوا بكنيتي، فإنما أنا قاسم)).
وزاد في لفظ:
((أقسم بينكم)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١١٥)، ومسلم (٢١٣٣: ٥).

14498 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Anṣārī narrated:
A man from among us had a son and named him al-Qāsim.
The Anṣār said to him:
“We will not give you the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, nor will we grant you the pleasure of being called by it.”
He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, a son was born to me and I named him al-Qāsim. The Anṣār said, ‘We will not give you the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, nor will we grant you that pleasure.’”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“The Anṣār have done well. Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah, for I am the one who distributes.”
Another wording adds:
“I distribute among you.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3115) and Muslim (2133:5).

١٤٥٠٠ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((تسموا باسمي، ولا تكتنوا بكنيتي، ومن رآني في المنام فقد رآني، فإن الشيطان لا يتمثل في صورتي، ومن كذب علي متعمدًا فليتبوأ مقعده من النار)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٩٧)، ومسلم (٢١٣٤، ٢٢٦٦: ٣).

“Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah. Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot assume my form. And whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6197) and Muslim (2134; 2266:3).

arabic_source:
١٤٥٠٥ — عن علي قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن ولد لي من بعدك ولد، أسميه باسمك وأكنيه كنيتك؟ قال:
((نعم)).
وزاد في لفظ: فكانت رخصة لي.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٦٧)، والترمذي (٢٨٤٣)، وأحمد (٧٣٠)، والحاكم (٤/٢٧٨).
أحاديث الأبواب السابقة تدل على كراهية التسمية بمحمد، مع التكنية بأبي القاسم في حياة رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وأما بعد مماته فكما جاز الجمع بينهما، جاز أيضًا التكنية بأبي القاسم لرفع المحظور عن ذلك في أصح أقوال أهل العلم.
وأما قول علي: “فكانت رخصة لي” فيظهر أنه من قول فطر بن خليفة الشيعي، وليس من كلام علي؛ لما جاء في مسند الإمام أحمد (٧٣٠): “فكانت رخصة من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لعلي”، وهو ظن منه وتخمين، ولذا مرة كان يذكره، وأخرى يسكت عنه، فإن أبا داود لم يذكر هذا القول.

english_source:
14505 — ʿAlī narrated:
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, if a son is born to me after you, may I name him with your name and give him your kunyah?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Another wording adds:
“That was a special permission for me.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4967), al-Tirmidhī (2843), Aḥmad (730), and al-Ḥākim (4/278).
The hadiths of the preceding chapters indicate the dislike of combining the name Muḥammad with the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
After his death, however, just as combining the two became permissible, taking the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim also became permissible because the reason for the restriction had ceased to exist, according to the strongest view among the scholars.
As for ʿAlī’s reported statement:
“That was a special permission for me,”
the author states that it appears to be from Fiṭr ibn Khalīfah rather than from ʿAlī himself.
In the Musnad of Imām Aḥmad (730), the wording is:
“It was a permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ʿAlī.”
The author considers this an inference and conjecture from Fiṭr, which is why he sometimes mentioned it and at other times omitted it.
Abū Dāwūd did not include this statement.

Zaynab had originally been named Barrah.
It was said:
“She is declaring herself righteous.”
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ renamed her Zaynab.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6192) and Muslim (2141).

((أنت جميلة)).
وفي رواية: أن ابنة لعمر كانت يقال لها عاصية… الحديث.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed the name ʿĀṣiyah and said:
“You are Jamīlah.”
In another narration:
A daughter of ʿUmar used to be called ʿĀṣiyah…
to the end of the hadith.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2139:14).

١٤٥١١ — عن مطيع بن الأسود قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول يوم فتح مكة:
((لا يقتل قرشي صبرًا بعد هذا اليوم إلى يوم القيامة)).
وزاد في رواية: ولم يكن أسلم أحد من عصاة قريش غير مطيع، كان اسمه العاصي فسماه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مطيعًا.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٧٨٢).

14511 — Muṭīʿ ibn al-Aswad narrated:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say on the day of the Conquest of Makkah:
“No Qurashī will be killed in captivity after this day until the Day of Resurrection.”
Another narration adds:
Of the men of Quraysh named al-ʿĀṣī, none had embraced Islam except Muṭīʿ. His name had been al-ʿĀṣī, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ renamed him Muṭīʿ.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1782).

١٤٥١٢ — عن سهل بن سعد قال: أتي بالمنذر بن أبي أسيد إلى النبي ﷺ حين ولد، فوضعه على فخذه، وأبو أسيد جالس، فلها النبي ﷺ شيء بين يديه، فأمر أبو أسيد بابنه، فاحتمل من فخذ النبي ﷺ، فاستفاق النبي ﷺ فقال:
((أين الصبي؟)).
فقال أبو أسيد: قلبناه يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((ما اسمه؟)).
قال: فلان. قال:
((ولكن اسمه المنذر)).
فسماه يومئذ المنذر.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٩١)، ومسلم (٢١٤٩).

14512 — Sahl ibn Saʿd narrated:
Al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd was brought to the Prophet ﷺ when he was born, and the Prophet ﷺ placed him upon his thigh while Abū Usayd was sitting nearby.
The Prophet ﷺ then became occupied with something before him, so Abū Usayd ordered that his son be taken away from the thigh of the Prophet ﷺ.
When the Prophet ﷺ became attentive again, he asked:
“Where is the child?”
Abū Usayd replied:
“We sent him back, O Messenger of Allah.”
He asked:
“What is his name?”
He replied:
“So-and-so.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Rather, his name is al-Mundhir.”
So he named him al-Mundhir that day.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6191) and Muslim (2149).

١٤٥١٣ — عن المسيب بن حزن أن أباه جاء إلى النبي ﷺ فقال:
((ما اسمك؟)).
قال: حزن. قال:
((أنت سهل)).
قال: لا أغير اسمًا سمانيه أبي. قال ابن المسيب: فما زالت الحزونة فينا بعد.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦١٩٠).
وقول سعيد: “فما زالت الحزونة” أي الغلظة والقساوة في خلقهم.

14513 — Al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn narrated that his father came to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What is your name?”
He replied:
“Ḥazn.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“You are Sahl.”
He replied:
“I will not change a name that my father gave me.”
Ibn al-Musayyib said:
“Harshness continued to remain among us afterward.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6190).
Saʿīd’s statement “harshness continued to remain among us” means roughness and severity in their character.

١٤٥١٤ — عن أسامة بن أخدري أن رجلًا يقال له أصرم كان في النفر الذين أتوا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ما اسمك؟)).
قال: أنا أصرم. قال:
((بل أنت زرعة)).
وفي لفظ: قال: أنت زرعة، فما تريد؟ قال: اسم هذا الغلام. قال:
((فهو عاصم)).
وقبض كفه.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٥٤)، والزيادة رواها الحاكم (٤/٢٧٦).

((بل أنت بشير)).

١٤٥١٨ — عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: لما ولد الحسن سماه حمزة، فلما ولد الحسين سماه بعمه جعفر. قال: فدعاني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((إني أمرت أن أغير اسم هذين)).
فقلت: اللّٰه ورسوله أعلم. فسماهما حسنًا وحسينًا.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٣٧٠) - واللفظ له -، والبزار (٦٥٧)، وأبو يعلى (٤٩٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٣/١٠٢).

english_source:
14518 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated:
When al-Ḥasan was born, I named him Ḥamzah.
When al-Ḥusayn was born, I named him after his paternal uncle Jaʿfar.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then called me and said:
“I have been commanded to change the names of these two.”
I replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
So he named them Ḥasan and Ḥusayn.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1370), and this is his wording, al-Bazzār (657), Abū Yaʿlā (498), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (3/102).

١٤٥٢٠ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: إن أمة لعمر رضي اللّٰه عنه كان لها اسم من أسماء العجم، فسماها عمر جميلة، فقالت لعمر: بيني وبينك النبي ﷺ. فأتينا النبي ﷺ فقال لها:
((أنت جميلة)).

14520 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
A female slave belonging to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, had a foreign name, so ʿUmar renamed her Jamīlah.
She said to ʿUmar:
“Let the Prophet ﷺ judge between you and me.”
So they went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to her:
“You are Jamīlah.”
ʿUmar then said:
“Take it, despite yourself.”

١٤٥٢١ — عن هانئ بن شريح قال: وفد إلى النبي ﷺ في قومه، فسمعهم يسمون رجلًا عبد الحجر، فقال له:
((ما اسمك؟)).
قال: عبد الحجر. فقال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إنما أنت عبد اللّٰه)).
حسن: رواه ابن أبي شيبة (٢٦٤٢١)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٨١١).

He came as part of a delegation from his people to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ heard them calling a man ʿAbd al-Ḥajar.

arabic_source:
١٤٥٢٢ — عن عائشة قالت: جاءت عجوز إلى النبي ﷺ، وهو عندي، فقال لها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من أنت؟)).
قالت: أنا جثامة المزنية. فقال:
((بل أنت حسانة المزنية، كيف أنتم؟ كيف حالكم؟ كيف كنتم بعدنا؟)).
قالت: بخير، بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول اللّٰه. فلما خرجت قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، تقبل على هذه العجوز هذا الإقبال؟ فقال:
((إنها كانت تأتينا زمن خديجة، وإن حسن العهد من الإيمان)).
حسن: رواه الحاكم (١/١٥-١٦)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٨٧٠١).

english_source:
14522 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
An elderly woman came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was with me.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked her:
“Who are you?”
She replied:
“I am Jathāmah al-Muzaniyyah.”
He said:
“Rather, you are Ḥassānah al-Muzaniyyah. How are you all? How is your condition? How have you been since we last saw you?”
She replied:
“We are well. May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah.”
When she left, I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, you showed this old woman such special attention?”
He replied:
“She used to visit us during the time of Khadījah, and indeed, faithfully maintaining old relationships is part of faith.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (1/15–16) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (8701).

١٤٥٢٣ — عن عتبة بن عبد السلمي قال: كان النبي ﷺ إذا أتاه الرجل وله الاسم لا يعجبه حوله، ولقد أتيناه تسعة من بني سليم، أكبرنا العرباض بن سارية، فبايعناه جميعًا معًا.
حسن: رواه ابن أبي عاصم في الآحاد والمثاني (١٣٦٥)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/١١٩).

14523 — ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī narrated:
When a man came to the Prophet ﷺ with a name that he did not like, he would change it.
Nine of us from Banū Sulaym came to him, the eldest of us being al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, and we all pledged allegiance to him together.
Good: Narrated by Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Āḥād wa-al-Mathānī (1365) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (17/119).

١٤٥٢٤ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن أخنع اسم عند اللّٰه رجل تسمى ملك الأملاك، لا مالك إلا اللّٰه عز وجل)).
وفي رواية:
((أخنى الأسماء يوم القيامة عند اللّٰه رجل تسمى ملك الأملاك)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٠٦)، ومسلم (٢١٤٣: ٢٠)، والرواية الثانية للبخاري (٦٢٠٥).
وقوله: “أخنى” من الخنا وهو الفحش في القول، وفسر “أخنع” أيضًا: بأذل، وبأفجر، وبأقبح. انظر: فتح الباري (١٠/٥٨٩).

١٤٥٢٧ — عن سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أحب الكلام إلى اللّٰه أربع: سبحان اللّٰه، والحمد للّٰه، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، لا يضرك بأيهن بدأت، ولا تسمين غلامك يسارًا، ولا رباحًا، ولا نجيحًا، ولا أفلح، فإنك تقول: أثم هو؟ فلا يكون، فيقول: لا، إنما هن أربع فلا تزيدن علي)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٣٧).

14527 — Samurah ibn Jundub narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The most beloved words to Allah are four: Subḥān Allah, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar. It does not matter with which of them you begin. And do not name your servant Yasār, Rabāḥ, Najīḥ, or Aflah, for you might ask, ‘Is he there?’ and he will not be there, so someone will answer, ‘No.’ They are only four, so do not add to them on my authority.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2137).

١٤٥٢٨ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه يقول: أراد النبي ﷺ أن ينهى عن أن يسمى بيعلى، وببركة، وبأفلح، وبيسار، وبنافع، وبنحو ذلك، ثم رأيته سكت بعد عنها، فلم يقل شيئًا، ثم قبض رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ولم ينه عن ذلك، ثم أراد عمر أن ينهى عن ذلك ثم تركه.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٣٨).
ورواه أبو داود (٤٩٦٠) من طريق الأعمش، عن أبي سفيان، عن جابر بلفظ:
((إن عشت - إن شاء اللّٰه - أنهى أمتي أن يسموا نافعًا، وأفلح، وبركة)).
قال الأعمش: ولا أدري ذكر نافعًا أم لا، فإن الرجل يقول: إذا جاء: أثم بركة؟ فيقولون: لا.

14528 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ intended to prohibit the names Yaʿlā, Barakah, Aflah, Yasār, Nāfiʿ, and similar names.
Then I later saw that he remained silent concerning them and said nothing further.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away without prohibiting them.
Later, ʿUmar intended to prohibit them, but then left the matter.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2138).
Abū Dāwūd (4960) also narrated through al-Aʿmash, from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, with the wording:
“If I live, Allah willing, I will prohibit my Ummah from naming children Nāfiʿ, Aflah, and Barakah.”
Al-Aʿmash said:
“I do not know whether he mentioned Nāfiʿ or not, for a man might come and ask, ‘Is Barakah there?’ and they would reply, ‘No.’”

١٤٥٢٩ — عن هانئ أنه لما وفد إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مع قومه سمعهم يكنونه بأبي الحكم، فدعاه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((إن اللّٰه هو الحكم، وإليه الحكم، فلم تكنى أبا الحكم؟)).
فقال: إن قومي إذا اختلفوا في شيء أتوني، فحكمت بينهم فرضي كلا الفريقين. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ما أحسن هذا، فما لك من الولد؟)).

14529 — Hāniʾ narrated:
When he came as part of a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his people, the Prophet ﷺ heard them calling him by the kunyah Abū al-Ḥakam.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said:
“Indeed, Allah is al-Ḥakam—the Judge—and judgment belongs to Him. Why are you called Abū al-Ḥakam?”
He replied:
“Whenever my people disagree about something, they come to me, and I judge between them, and both sides are satisfied.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“How excellent this is. What children do you have?”
He replied:
“I have Shurayḥ, Muslim, and ʿAbdullāh.”
He asked:
“Which of them is the eldest?”
I replied:
“Shurayḥ.”
He said:
“Then you are Abū Shurayḥ.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4955) and al-Nasāʾī (5387), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (504), and narrated by al-Ḥākim (4/279) through another route.

١٤٥٣٠ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أحسن الناس خلقًا، وكان لي أخ يقال له: أبو عمير، قال: أحسبه، قال: كان فطيمًا، قال: فكان إذا جاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فرآه، قال:
((يا أبا عمير، ما فعل النغير؟)).
قال: فكان يلعب به.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٠٣)، ومسلم (٢١٥٠).

14530 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the best of people in character.
I had a little brother who was called Abū ʿUmayr. I think he had already been weaned.
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and saw him, he would say:
“O Abū ʿUmayr, what happened to the little nughayr?”
The child used to play with that small bird.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6203) and Muslim (2150).

١٤٥٣١ — عن أم خالد بنت خالد: أتي النبي ﷺ بثياب فيها خميصة سوداء صغيرة، فقال:
((من ترون أن نكسو هذه؟)).
فسكت القوم. قال:
((ائتوني بأم خالد)).
فأتي بها تحمل، فأخذ الخميصة بيده فألبسها، وقال:
((أبلي وأخلقي)).
وكان فيها علم أخضر أو أصفر، فقال:
((يا أم خالد، هذا سناه)).
وسناه بالحبشية: حسن.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٨٢٣).
قوله: “فأتي بها تحمل” قال الحافظ: فيه إشارة إلى صغر سنها إذ ذاك، لكن لا يمنع ذلك أن تكون حينئذ مميزة.
قوله: “أبلي وأخلقي” الأمر بالإبلاء والإخلاق وهما بمعنى، والعرب تطلق ذلك وتريد الدعاء بطول البقاء للمخاطب بذلك، أي أنها تطول حياتها حتى يبلى الثوب ويخلق.
ووقع في رواية: “وأخلفي” بالفاء بدل القاف. قال الحافظ: وهي أوجه؛ لأن الأولى تستلزم التأييد، والثانية تفيد معنى زائدًا، وهو أنها إذا أبلته أخلفت غيره. انظر: الفتح (١٠/٢٨٠).

14531 — Umm Khālid bint Khālid narrated:
Some garments were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, among them a small black patterned cloak.
He asked:
“Who do you think we should dress in this?”
The people remained silent.
He said:
“Bring me Umm Khālid.”
She was brought while being carried.
The Prophet ﷺ took the cloak in his hand, dressed her in it, and said:
“Wear it until it becomes worn out.”
The garment had a green or yellow design on it.
He said:
“O Umm Khālid, this is sanāh.”
In the Abyssinian language, sanāh means “beautiful.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5823).
Regarding the words “she was brought while being carried,” al-Ḥāfiẓ said that this indicates how young she was at the time, though it does not prevent her from having already reached an age of discernment.
The words “Abli wa akhliqī” are an Arabic expression used as a supplication for long life, meaning: may you live long enough for the garment to become worn and old.
Another narration reads “wa akhlifī” with an fāʾ instead of a qāf.
Al-Ḥāfiẓ said this wording is more appropriate, because the first could imply perpetuity, whereas the second adds the meaning that after she wears this garment out, she will receive another in its place.
See Fatḥ al-Bārī (10/280).

((يا عائش، هذا جبريل يقرئك السلام)).

١٤٥٣٣ — عن أنس قال: كانت أم سليم في الثقل، وأنجشة غلام النبي ﷺ يسوق بهن، فقال النبي ﷺ:
((يا أنجش، رويدك سوقك بالقوارير)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٠٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٢٣: ٧١)، واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم: «يا أنجشة».

Umm Sulaym was among the women traveling with the caravan, and Anjashah, a servant of the Prophet ﷺ, was driving their camels.

١٤٥٣٤ — عن سهل بن سعد قال: إن كانت أحب أسماء علي إليه لأبو تراب، وإن كان ليفرح أن يدعى بها، وما سماه أبو تراب إلا النبي ﷺ. غاضب يومًا فاطمة، فخرج، فاضطجع إلى الجدار إلى المسجد، فجاءه النبي ﷺ يتبعه، فقيل: هو ذا مضطجع في الجدار. فجاءه النبي ﷺ وامتلأ ظهره ترابًا، فجعل النبي ﷺ يمسح التراب عن ظهره ويقول:
((اجلس يا أبا تراب)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٠٤)، ومسلم (٢٤٠٩).

english_source:
14534 — Sahl ibn Saʿd narrated:
Of all the names by which ʿAlī was called, the one most beloved to him was Abū Turāb, and he would be happy when he was called by it.
No one gave him the name Abū Turāb except the Prophet ﷺ.
One day, there was some disagreement between him and Fāṭimah, so he went out and lay down beside a wall near the mosque.
The Prophet ﷺ came looking for him and was told:
“There he is, lying beside the wall.”
The Prophet ﷺ came to him and found that his back had become covered with dust.
He began wiping the dust from his back and saying:
“Sit up, O Abū Turāb.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6204) and Muslim (2409).

١٤٥٣٥ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: يا رسول اللّٰه، كل صواحبي لهن كنى. قال:
((فاكتني بابنك عبد اللّٰه)).
يعني ابن أختها، وهو عبد اللّٰه بن الزبير. قال: فكانت تكنى بأم عبد اللّٰه.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٧٠)، وأحمد (٢٤٧٥٦).

14535 — ʿĀʾishah said:
“O Messenger of Allah, all of my companions have kunyahs.”
He said:
“Then take the kunyah from your son ʿAbdullāh.”
He meant her sister’s son, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr.
So she became known by the kunyah Umm ʿAbdullāh.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4970) and Aḥmad (24756).

I brought Ibn al-Zubayr to the Prophet ﷺ.
He performed taḥnīk for him with a date and said:
“This is ʿAbdullāh, and you are Umm ʿAbdullāh.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (24619) and al-Ḥākim (4/278).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him the kunyah Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, even though no child had yet been born to him.

١٤٥٣٨ — عن حمزة بن صهيب أن عمر قال لصهيب: ما لك تكتني بأبي يحيى، وليس لك ولد؟ قال: كناني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بأبي يحيى.
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٣٧٣٨)، وأحمد (٢٣٩٢٦).

١٤٥٣٩ — عن أسامة بن زيد أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ركب على حمار عليه قطيفة فدكية، وأسامة وراءه، يعود سعد بن عبادة في بني حارث بن الخزرج، قبل وقعة بدر. فسارا حتى مرا بمجلس فيه عبد اللّٰه بن أبي ابن سلول، وذلك قبل أن يسلم عبد اللّٰه بن أبي، فإذا في المجلس أخلاط من المسلمين والمشركين عبدة الأوثان واليهود، وفي المسلمين عبد اللّٰه بن رواحة. فلما غشيت المجلس عجاجة الدابة، خمر ابن أبي أنفه بردائه وقال: لا تغبروا علينا. فسلم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ عليهم ثم وقف، فنزل فدعاهم إلى اللّٰه وقرأ عليهم القرآن. فقال له عبد اللّٰه بن أبي ابن سلول: أيها المرء، لا أحسن مما تقول إن كان حقًا، فلا تؤذنا به في مجالسنا، فمن جاءك فاقصص عليه. قال عبد اللّٰه بن رواحة: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه، فاغشنا في مجالسنا، فإنا نحب ذلك. فاستب المسلمون والمشركون واليهود حتى كادوا يتثاورون، فلم يزل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يخفضهم حتى سكتوا، ثم ركب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ دابته، فسار حتى دخل على سعد بن عبادة، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أي سعد، ألم تسمع ما قال أبو حباب - يريد عبد اللّٰه بن أبي - قال كذا وكذا)).
… الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٠٧)، ومسلم (١٧٩٨).

14539 — Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode a donkey upon which was a Fadakī cloak, with Usāmah riding behind him, on his way to visit Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah among Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj before the Battle of Badr.
They passed by a gathering in which ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl was present, before he had outwardly accepted Islam.
The gathering contained a mixture of Muslims, idol-worshipping polytheists, and Jews. Among the Muslims was ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah.
When the dust raised by the animal reached the gathering, Ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said:
“Do not cover us with dust.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them salām, stopped, dismounted, called them to Allah, and recited the Qur’an to them.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said:
“O man, nothing could be better than what you say if it is true. But do not disturb us with it in our gatherings. Whoever comes to you, tell it to him.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah said:
“Rather, O Messenger of Allah, come to us in our gatherings, for we love that.”
The Muslims, polytheists, and Jews then began insulting one another until they almost came to blows.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued calming them until they fell silent.
Then he mounted his animal and went to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O Saʿd, did you not hear what Abū Ḥubāb said?”
meaning ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy.
Then he mentioned what he had said.
…to the end of the hadith.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6207) and Muslim (1798).

١٤٥٤٠ — عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، أن عمر بن الخطاب ضرب ابنًا له يكنى أبا عيسى، وأن المغيرة بن شعبة تكنى بأبي عيسى، فقال له عمر: أما يكفيك أن تكنى بأبي عبد اللّٰه؟ فقال: إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كناني. فقال: إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قد غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، وإنا في جلجتنا. فلم يزل يكنى بأبي عبد اللّٰه حتى هلك.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٦٣)، والضياء في المختارة (٨٦)، والحاكم (٣/٤٧٧) مختصراً.

14540 — Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from his father:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb disciplined one of his sons who had taken the kunyah Abū ʿĪsā.
Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah also used the kunyah Abū ʿĪsā.
ʿUmar said to him:
“Is it not enough for you to take the kunyah Abū ʿAbdullāh?”
Al-Mughīrah replied:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me that kunyah.”
ʿUmar said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had his past and future sins forgiven, while we remain in our uncertain condition.”
Al-Mughīrah continued to be called Abū ʿAbdullāh until he died.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4963), al-Ḍiyāʾ in al-Mukhtārah (86), and al-Ḥākim (3/477) in a shortened wording.

“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had his past and future sins forgiven, while we remain in our uncertain condition.”
Al-Mughīrah continued to be called Abū ʿAbdullāh until he died.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4963), al-Ḍiyāʾ in al-Mukhtārah (86), and al-Ḥākim (3/477) in a shortened wording.

14541 — Abū Jubayrah ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated:
This verse was revealed concerning us, Banū Salamah:
“And do not insult one another by offensive nicknames. How evil it is to be called by a sinful name after having faith.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:11]
He said:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, there was hardly a man among us who did not have two or three names.
The Prophet ﷺ would call someone:
“O so-and-so.”
The people would say:
“Stop, O Messenger of Allah. He becomes angry when called by that name.”
So this verse was revealed:
“And do not call one another by offensive nicknames.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4962), al-Tirmidhī (3268), Ibn Mājah (3741), Aḥmad (18288), and al-Ḥākim (4/281–282).

١٤٥٤٢ — عن حذيفة قال: كنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((أحصوا لي كم يلفظ الإسلام)).
قال: فقلنا: يا رسول اللّٰه، أتخاف علينا ونحن ما بين الستمائة إلى السبعمائة؟ قال:
((إنكم لا تدرون، لعلكم أن تبتلوا)).
قال: فابتلينا حتى جعل الرجل منا لا يصلي إلا سرًا.
وفي لفظ: “فكتبنا له ألفًا وخمسمائة رجل، فقلنا: نخاف ونحن ألف وخمسمائة”.
متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١٤٩: ٢٣٥)، والبخاري (٣٠٦٠).

english_source:
14542 — Ḥudhayfah narrated:
We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said:
“Count for me how many people profess Islam.”
We said:
“O Messenger of Allah, do you fear for us when we are between six hundred and seven hundred?”
He replied:
“You do not know. Perhaps you will be tested.”
Ḥudhayfah said:
“And indeed we were tested, until a man among us could only pray secretly.”
In another wording:
“We recorded for him the names of one thousand five hundred men, and we said: ‘Should we still fear when we are one thousand five hundred?’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (149:235) and al-Bukhārī (3060).

١٤٥٤٣ — عن أبي ذر أنه سمع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((ليس من رجل ادعى لغير أبيه وهو يعلمه إلا كفر، ومن ادعى ما ليس له فليس منا، وليتبوأ مقعده من النار، ومن دعا رجلًا بالكفر، أو قال: عدو اللّٰه، وليس كذلك، إلا حار عليه)).
وفي لفظ البخاري:
((ومن ادعى قومًا ليس فيهم فليتبوأ مقعده من النار)).
متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (٦١)، والبخاري (٣٥٠٨، ٦٠٤٥).

14543 — Abū Dharr narrated that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No man knowingly claims another man as his father except that he has committed an act of kufr. Whoever claims what does not belong to him is not from us, and let him take his seat in the Fire. And whoever calls another man a disbeliever or says, ‘Enemy of Allah,’ when he is not such, then that accusation returns upon him.”
In al-Bukhārī’s wording:
“Whoever claims to belong to a people when he is not one of them, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (61) and al-Bukhārī (3508, 6045).

14544 — Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the greatest fabrications is for a man to claim lineage to someone other than his father, to claim that his eyes saw what they did not see, or to attribute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something that he did not say.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3509).

١٤٥٤٧ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال: ما سأل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أحد عن الدجال أكثر مما سألته عنه، فقال لي:
((أي بني، وما ينصبك منه؟ إنه لن يضرك)).
قال: قلت: إنهم يزعمون أن معه أنهار الماء وجبال الخبز. قال:
((هو أهون على اللّٰه من ذلك)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٥٢).

14547 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah narrated:
No one asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more questions about the Dajjāl than I did.
He said to me:
“My son, why are you so troubled by him? He will not harm you.”
I said:
“They claim that he will have rivers of water and mountains of bread with him.”
He replied:
“He is far more insignificant to Allah than that.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2152).

((إذا جمع اللّٰه الأولين والآخرين يوم القيامة، يرفع لكل غادر لواء، فقيل: هذه غدرة فلان بن فلان)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٧٧)، ومسلم (١٧٣٥: ٩)، واللفظ لمسلم.

14548 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every betrayer, and it will be said: ‘This is the betrayal of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6177) and Muslim (1735:9). The wording is that of Muslim.

((إن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة، ما يتبين ما فيها، يهوي بها في النار أبعد ما بين المشرق والمغرب)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٤٧٧)، ومسلم (٢٩٨٨)، واللفظ لمسلم، ولم يذكر البخاري: «والمغرب».

14549 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A servant may utter a word without considering what it contains, and because of it he falls into the Fire farther than the distance between the east and the west.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6477) and Muslim (2988). The wording is that of Muslim; al-Bukhārī did not mention “and the west.”

١٤٥٥٠ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة من رضوان اللّٰه، لا يلقي لها بالًا، يرفعه اللّٰه بها درجات، وإن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة من سخط اللّٰه، لا يلقي لها بالًا، يهوي بها في جهنم)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٤٧٨).

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6478).

١٤٥٥٣ — عن أبي موسى قال: كنت أنا وأبو الدرداء عند رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((من حفظ ما بين فقميه ورجليه دخل الجنة)).
حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (٧٢٧٥)، والحاكم (٤/٣٥٨)، والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٥٣٧١).

“Whoever guards what is between his two jaws and what is between his two legs will enter Paradise.”

The word al-fuqm, with a ḍammah on the fāʾ, means the beard.

١٤٥٥٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سئل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ عن أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة؟ فقال:
((تقوى اللّٰه وحسن الخلق)).
وسئل عن أكثر ما يدخل الناس النار؟ فقال:
((الفم والفرج)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٠٠٤)، وابن حبان (٤٧٦)، والحاكم (٤/٣٢٤).

14555 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked:
“What most often causes people to enter Paradise?”
He replied:
“Taqwā of Allah and good character.”
He was asked:
“What most often causes people to enter the Fire?”
He replied:
“The mouth and the private parts.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2004), Ibn Ḥibbān (476), and al-Ḥākim (4/324).

14556 — ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A person’s good fortune and bad fortune lie in what is between his two jaws.”
Wahb said:
“He means his tongue.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5717) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (17/85).

“Whoever remains silent is saved.”

١٤٥٥٨ — عن سفيان بن عبد اللّٰه الثقفي قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، حدثني بأمر أعتصم به. قال:
((قل ربي اللّٰه ثم استقم)).
قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما أخوف ما تخاف علي؟ فأخذ بلسان نفسه، ثم قال:
((هذا)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٤١٠)، وابن ماجه (٣٩٧٢)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥٦٩٩)، والحاكم (٤/٣١٣).

14558 — Sufyān ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Thaqafī narrated:
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, tell me something to which I may firmly hold.”
He said:
“Say: ‘My Lord is Allah,’ then remain steadfast.”
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?”
He took hold of his own tongue and said:
“This.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2410), Ibn Mājah (3972), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5699), and al-Ḥākim (4/313).

١٤٥٥٩ — عن بلال بن الحارث المزني، صاحب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، يقول: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((إن أحدكم ليتكلم بالكلمة من رضوان اللّٰه ما يظن أن تبلغ ما بلغت، فيكتب اللّٰه له بها رضوانه إلى يوم يلقاه، وإن أحدكم ليتكلم بالكلمة من سخط اللّٰه ما يظن أن تبلغ ما بلغت، فيكتب اللّٰه عليه بها سخطه إلى يوم يلقاه)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٣١٩)، وابن ماجه (٢٦٦٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٢٨٠)، والحاكم (١/٤٥)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٤٦٠٦).

14559 — Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“One of you may utter a word pleasing to Allah, not realizing how far its effect will reach, and because of it Allah records His pleasure for him until the day he meets Him. And one of you may utter a word angering Allah, not realizing how far its effect will reach, and because of it Allah records His anger against him until the day he meets Him.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2319), Ibn Mājah (2669), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (280), al-Ḥākim (1/45), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (4606).

حسن: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (٢٣٢٣).

((ليس شيء من الجسد إلا يشكو ذرب اللسان على حدته)).
حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (٥)، وعنه ابن السني في عمل اليوم والليلة (٧)، وابن أبي الدنيا في الصمت (١٣)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٤٥٩٦).

“There is no part of the body except that it complains of the tongue because of the sharpness of its speech.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (5), and through him by Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-al-Laylah (7), Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Ṣamt (13), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (4596).

((لا تكثروا الكلام بغير ذكر اللّٰه، فإن كثرة الكلام بغير ذكر اللّٰه قسوة للقلب، وإن أبعد الناس من اللّٰه القلب القاسي)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٤١١)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٤٦٠٠).

“Do not speak excessively without the remembrance of Allah, for excessive speech without the remembrance of Allah hardens the heart, and the person farthest from Allah is the one with a hard heart.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2411) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (4600).

١٤٥٦٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود أنه ارتقى الصفا فأخذ بلسانه، فقال: يا لسان، قل خيرًا تغنم، واسكت عن شر تسلم، من قبل أن تندم. ثم قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((أكثر خطايا ابن آدم في لسانه)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (١٠/٢٤٣)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٤/١٠٧).

14563 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd climbed al-Ṣafā and took hold of his tongue.
He said:
“O tongue, speak good and you will profit; remain silent from evil and you will be safe, before you come to regret.”
Then he said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Most of the sins of the son of Adam are committed by his tongue.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (10/243) and Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ (4/107).

arabic_source:
١٤٥٦٤ — عن أسود بن أصرم المحاربي أنه قدم بإبل له سمان إلى المدينة في زمن قحل وجدوب من الأرض، فلما رآها أهل المدينة عجبوا من سمنها، فذكرت ذلك للرسول ﷺ، فأرسل إليها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأتي بها، فخرج إليها فنظر إليها، فقال:
((لم جلبت إبلك هذه؟)).
قال: أردت بها خادمًا. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من عنده خادم؟)).
فقال عثمان بن عفان رضي اللّٰه عنه: عندي يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((فائت بها)).
فجاء بها عثمان، فلما رآها أسود قال: مثلها أريد. فقال:
((عندك فخذها)).
فأخذها أسود، وقبض رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إبله. فقال أسود: يا رسول اللّٰه، أوصني. قال:
((هل تملك لسانك؟)).
قال: فما أملك إذا لم أملكه؟ قال:
((أفتملك يدك؟)).
قال: فماذا أملك إذا لم أملك يدي؟ قال:
((فلا تقل بلسانك إلا معروفًا، ولا تبسط يدك إلا إلى خير)).
صحيح: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (١/٢٥٦-٢٥٧)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٤٥٨٣).

14564 — Aswad ibn Aṣram al-Muḥāribī came to Madinah with some very fat camels during a time of drought and barrenness.
When the people of Madinah saw them, they were amazed at how fat they were.
This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sent for the camels.
They were brought, and he went out and looked at them.
He asked:
“Why have you brought these camels?”
Aswad replied:
“I want to exchange them for a servant.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who has a servant?”
ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, said:
“I do, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Bring her.”
ʿUthmān brought her.
When Aswad saw her, he said:
“This is the kind I want.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“She is yours, so take her.”
Aswad took her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received his camels.
Aswad then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, advise me.”
He said:
“Can you control your tongue?”
Aswad replied:
“What could I control if I cannot control my tongue?”
He said:
“Can you control your hand?”
Aswad replied:
“What could I control if I cannot control my hand?”
He said:
“Then say nothing with your tongue except what is good, and extend your hand only toward what is good.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (1/256–257) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (4583).

((نعم)).

((الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه)).

((نعم الشيء الجهاد، والذي بالناس أملك من ذلك فالصيام والصدقة)).
قال:
((نعم الشيء الصيام والصدقة)).

14565 — ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated:
One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out riding his mount, with his Companions traveling with him.
Muʿādh ibn Jabal said:
“O Prophet of Allah, will you permit me, if you are pleased, to come closer to you?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Muʿādh came near him, and they traveled together.
Muʿādh said:
“May my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. I ask Allah to make our day of death come before yours. If something should happen—and we hope, Allah willing, that nothing will—what deeds should we perform after you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent, then said:
“Jihād in the path of Allah.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Jihād is indeed an excellent thing, but something more within people’s ability than that is fasting and charity.”
He said:
“Fasting and charity are excellent things.”
Muʿādh then mentioned every kind of good deed that the son of Adam performs.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There is something even better for people than that.”
Muʿādh asked:
“What could be better than that, O Prophet of Allah?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pointed toward his mouth and said:
“Silence, except when speaking good.”
Muʿādh asked:
“Will we really be held accountable for what our tongues say?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck Muʿādh’s thigh and said:
“O Muʿādh, may your mother lose you—or whatever expression Allah willed him to say—what else throws people onto their faces in Hell except what their tongues have uttered? Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent from evil. Speak good and you will profit; remain silent from evil and you will be safe.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (4/286–287), and this is his wording, and by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr, as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Jāmiʿ al-Masānīd (4914).

١٤٥٦٦ — عن أبي شريح الكعبي أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((من كان يؤمن باللّٰه واليوم الآخر، فليقل خيرًا أو ليصمت، ومن كان يؤمن باللّٰه واليوم الآخر، فليكرم جاره، ومن كان يؤمن باللّٰه واليوم الآخر، فليكرم ضيفه، جائزته يوم وليلة، وضيافته ثلاثة أيام، فما كان بعد ذلك فهو صدقة، ولا يحل له أن يثوي عنده حتى يحرجه)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في صفة النبي ﷺ (٢٢)، والبخاري في الأدب (٦١٣٥) من طريق مالك به. ورواه البخاري (٦٠١٩)، ومسلم (٤٨: ١٤) عقب الحديث (١٧٢٦).

14566 — Abū Shurayḥ al-Kaʿbī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest. His special hospitality is for one day and one night, and hospitality is for three days. Whatever comes after that is charity. And it is not lawful for the guest to remain with him until he causes him hardship.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ṣifat al-Nabī ﷺ (22), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab (6135) through Mālik, and also by al-Bukhārī (6019) and Muslim (48:14) after Hadith 1726.

١٤٥٦٧ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ثلاث مرار:
((رحم اللّٰه امرأ تكلم فغنم، أو سكت فسلم)).
حسن: رواه البيهقي في الشعب (٤٥٨٩)، وابن أبي الدنيا في الصمت (٤١).
قوله: “تكلم فغنم، أو سكت فسلم” يعني: تكلم بخير فغنم بالأجر والثواب، أو سكت عن الشر فسلم من الوزر والعقاب.

14567 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said three times:
“May Allah have mercy on a person who speaks and thereby gains, or remains silent and thereby remains safe.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (4589) and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Ṣamt (41).
The words:
“speaks and thereby gains, or remains silent and thereby remains safe”
mean that he speaks good and thereby gains reward and recompense, or remains silent from evil and is thereby saved from sin and punishment.

١٤٥٦٨ — عن عدي بن حاتم، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه ذكر النار فتعوذ منها، وأشاح بوجهه ثلاث مرار، ثم قال:
((اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة، فإن لم تجدوا، فبكلمة طيبة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠٢٣)، ومسلم (١٠١٦: ٦٨)، واللفظ لمسلم.

14568 — ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Fire, sought refuge from it, and turned his face away three times.
Then he said:
“Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date. If you cannot find even that, then with a good word.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6023) and Muslim (1016:68). The wording is that of Muslim.

١٤٥٦٩ — عن صهيب قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا صلى العصر همس.
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٣٤٠).
قوله: “الهمس” هو الصوت الخفي. قال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا﴾ [سورة طه: ١٠٨].

english_source:
14569 — Ṣuhayb narrated:
“When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed ʿAṣr, he would speak softly.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3340).
The word “al-hams” means a low or subdued voice.
Allah, the Exalted, says:
“And all voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a faint whisper.”
 [Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:108]

١٤٥٧٠ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن اللّٰه عز وجل يبغض البليغ من الرجال الذي يتخلل بلسانه تخلل الباقرة بلسانها)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٠٥)، والترمذي (٢٨٥٣)، وأحمد (٦٥٤٣).
قوله: “يبغض البليغ من الرجال” أي المبالغة في الكلام وأداء الحروف.
وقوله: “يتخلل” أي يتشدق في الكلام، ويفخم لسانه، ويلفه كما تلف البقرة بلسانها.

14570 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates the overly eloquent man who twists and rolls his tongue in speech as a cow rolls its tongue.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5005), al-Tirmidhī (2853), and Aḥmad (6543).
The phrase “the eloquent man” here refers to one who exaggerates in his speech and in the articulation of letters.
The words “twists his tongue” mean that he speaks with affectation, exaggerates the movements of his tongue, and rolls it in an ostentatious manner, like a cow moving its tongue.

وقوله: “يتخلل” أي يتشدق في الكلام، ويفخم لسانه، ويلفه كما تلف البقرة بلسانها.
14570 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates the overly eloquent man who twists and rolls his tongue in speech as a cow rolls its tongue.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5005), al-Tirmidhī (2853), and Aḥmad (6543).
The phrase “the eloquent man” here refers to one who exaggerates in his speech and in the articulation of letters.
The words “twists his tongue” mean that he speaks with affectation, exaggerates the movements of his tongue, and rolls it in an ostentatious manner, like a cow moving its tongue.

١٤٥٧٢ — عن أبي وائل قال: خطبنا عمار فأوجز وأبلغ، فلما نزل قلنا: يا أبا اليقظان، لقد أبلغت وأوجزت، فلو كنت تنفست! فقال: إني سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((إن طول صلاة الرجل وقصر خطبته مئنة من فقهه، فأطيلوا الصلاة، وأقصروا الخطبة، وإن من البيان لسحرًا)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٨٦٩).
قوله: “مئنة” بميم مفتوحة، ثم همزة مكسورة، ثم نون مشددة، مشتق من “أنَّ” الذي هو حرف تأكيد وتحقيق، والخطبة هي الموضع الذي يتحقق فيه أن المتكلم فقيه.

english_source:
14572 — Abū Wāʾil narrated:
ʿAmmār delivered a sermon to us that was brief yet eloquent.
When he stepped down, we said:
“O Abū al-Yaqẓān, you spoke eloquently and concisely. If only you had spoken a little longer!”
He replied:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“The length of a man’s prayer and the brevity of his sermon are signs of his understanding. So lengthen the prayer and shorten the sermon, and indeed some eloquence is like magic.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (869).
The word “miʾinnah” begins with an open mīm, followed by a kasrah on the hamzah and a doubled nūn. It conveys the meaning of a sign or indication establishing something with certainty.
Thus, the sermon is a place in which a speaker’s understanding may become evident.
